Question: How old is Romania?
Answer: Romania has been settled and occupied at least since 35,000 B.C. Skull of inhabitant of Romania circa 35,000 B.C. Romania history is a long and interesting one. Evidence of modern humans have been found in modern day Romania dating back to 34,950 B.C. Neolithic Romania The Neolithic period of ancient Romania lasted from 10.000 BC to 2000 BC. The Neolithic people were indigenous Europeans who were later conquered by the Indo-Europeans. The indigenous people of Neolithic cultures from present-day Romania are believed to have mixed with Proto-Indo-Europeans, giving birth to proto-Thracians from which Thracians and Dacians developed later on. Thracians The intermixing of Indo-Europeans and these Neolithic farmers became known as Thracians. These Thracians first settled in the Danube-Carthpathian region of Romania. The area transformed into the Kingdom of Dacia by Burebista (c. 80-44 B.C.), who conquered and united several other Dacian principalities. Dacia under Burebista The Dacians had periods of independence and were also controlled by invading forces such as the Celts, Persians and eventually came into conflict with the Roman Empire. Dacia was an independent kingdom that Rome had long desired. Several campaigns were launched against the Independent Kingdom but none were completely successful. Rome greatly desired the bountiful amount of salt which was plentiful in Dacia. Salt was a necessity in the ancient world because it helped preserve meat and fish in a world before refrigerators. Salt was incredibly plentiful in Dacia so much that there are salt mines even there today. Many people incorrectly believe Dacia was invaded because of its gold but Rome only discovered the copious amounts of the precious metal after their invasion by accident. When the Romans decisively attacked Dacia, the locals hid this lucrative treasure in a riverbed by diverting the river from its course. The Romans only happened upon this fortune years later. The Dacians often entered Roman territory and plundered wherever they went. Eventually the Roman Emperor Trajen launched two military campaigns against Dacia that were ultimately successful in 101-102 and 105-106 A.D. Campaign of Dacia by the Emperor Trajan Trajan and his legions crushed the forces of Dacia and completely occupied the kingdom. To stamp out any attempt at rebellion, the Romans made slaves of the population of Dacia and sent them to the far corners of the Empire. As history reveals, the policy of the Romans was to colonize every foreign country they had conquered by war in order that the conquest might last and a further expansion of the Roman Empire be possible. This policy was also followed by Trajan with the Dacians by colonizing their land with Roman soldiers and Roman officials. In fact, the entire administration of Dacia was Roman. Besides the Roman legions and officials, another element came to Dacia: Roman merchants who usually followed their armies. The Kingdom of Dacia was completely changed linguistically and ethnically. Most of the modern day Romanians can trace their heritage to a mixture of Roman and Thracian culture and peoples. This is why the Romanian language is a Romance language because it originates from Vulgar Latin, which is a subgroup of the Italic branch of the Indo-European language family. The Romans eventually abandoned Dacia in 271 A.D. when they grew tired of fighting the rebellious Dacians and the barbaric Goths who invaded the province from the east. Marcus Aurelius decided to abandon Dacia completely. I won’t go into the history of modern day Romania after the Romans abandoned the Territory Because it would make this answer way too long. Question: Why did so many soldiers have to get their limbs amputated during the American Civil War?
Answer: Because one, the bullets that soldiers used in the Civil War were heavier and shattered bones rather than passing through the body and two because of massive infections As I mentioned above, the bullet used by soldiers during the Civil War was called the Minie ball. The Minie Ball by modern standards was enormous. It weighed 1 ½ ounces and these rather large bullets (.58 caliber) were propelled relatively slowly by the black powder charge. The Minie Ball was a conical bullet with hollowed grooves. When it struck a human, the ball caused considerable damage, oftentimes flattening upon impact. Minie balls splintered bones, damaged muscle, and drove dirt, clothing, and other debris into the wounds. This of course created two massive problems. One, the bones more often than not shattered rather than a clean break and second, infections were commonplace. Over the course of the Civil War, three out of four surgeries (or close to 60,000 operations) were amputations. The powerful heavy Minie Ball had a tremendous amount of crushing power and that crushing power translated into bones that were not simply broken, but rather they were shattered. Now in today's modern world, that's not a problem. We can put you into an x-ray machine, take a look at where all the broken pieces went, remove them from your body and save your life. But in the 19th Century, doctors had literally no idea how to repair or set shattered bones. An even bigger problem was infection and gangrene. There was no soap or antibiotics and cutting off limbs was the best way to stave off further infection and gangrene from spreading. Doctors were also accused of taking unnecessary steps or unnecessary surgeries to hone their skills and learn from their failures. “Critics, like Confederate surgeon Julian John Chisholm, charged that inexperienced doctors were too eager to attempt amputation as a way to improve their skills, and accused them of experimenting, often exacerbating existing injuries. Soldiers nicknamed such enthusiasts "butchers" and some even went so far as to treat themselves to try to avoid the painful intervention of the surgeon.” -Source: History of Medicine Finally, contrary to popular belief, anesthesia was available and widely used during the Civil War. “Anesthesia was an important surgical advance introduced a few decades before the Civil War. Ether or chloroform was applied to a cloth cone that was placed over the mouth and nose of the patient. The patient became stuporous in a matter of minutes.” “This state lasted for more than enough time to perform an amputation, which took about 6 minutes to complete. Union surgeons used anesthesia in more than 80,000 operations.” -Source: To Bind Up the Nations Wounds For all the aforementioned reasons, thousands of amputations were performed during the Civil War. I hope that clears up any confusion! I 💖C2, questions, disagreements, curses and hexes! -Jason

Question: What is the machete order for watching Star Wars and is it worth considering?
Answer: The Machete Order is watching the Star Wars movies so that you don’t ruin the surprise of Darth Vader/Anakin’s reveal and to make a better viewing experience The Machete Order of watching Star Wars movies is: A New Hope, The Empire Strikes Back, Attack of the Clones, Revenge of the Sith, Return of the Jedi and then The Force Awakens, The Last Jedi and The Rise of Skywalker. Yes, you read the list right, Episode I: The Phantom Menace is not included. Supposedly by watching the films in this order, you not only avoid any spoilers, but maintain the original narrative’s focus. And by that I mean you’re supposed to have Luke Skywalker be the centerpiece of all the movies. So you follow his journey from a New Hope and coming of age to the Empire Strikes Back and then the great reveal that he finds out that his father is in fact Darth Vader. The thinking is you preserve the father reveal, Luke is the central narrative and you don’t ruin the Force Ghost redemption story. Meaning seeing Hayden Christianson’s Force Ghost rather than Sebastian Shaw won’t confuse the audience. And why is the Phantom Menace left out? Because the movie has no effect on the Luke narrative, the story is superfluous to the overall Skywalker saga and young Anakin’s actions are irrelevant to the overall saga. Darth Maul has no bearing upon the movies and is replaced by Count Dooku. Equally, Qui-Gon Jinn's actions have no bearing outside the movie. All characters who pass over to Episode II are also re-introduced along with their motives. Also, by dropping young Anakin, Luke’s story arc is paralleled with Anakin’s. It makes Yoda’s warning to Luke about the power of the Emperor that much more pointant. It also makes Luke’s switch to all black and his Force Choke to the Gamorrean Guard remind you of Anakin’s Force Choke of Padme. But in my personal opinion, it may be worth considering, but honestly, the Machete Order seems rather silly to me and unnecessary. It also discounts Obi-Wan‘s journey from Padawan to Knight and Master in the Phantom Menace as if it doesn’t matter which is entirely untrue. As well as the fact, it also discounts any of the other supplemental material like the Clone Wars animated series and stand alone movies like Solo (which brought back Darth Maul) and Rebels. If you remove the Phantom Menace you lose all that and you also lose Palpatine’s beginnings in politics and his rise to power. I also think having an audience go from watching Empire Strikes Back (arguably the best Star Wars movies) to Attack of the Clones (one of the worst) makes a terrible cinematic experience. The Machete Order is supposed to enhance your viewing of the movies and yet I think its order would actually take away from the overall story and the beauty of the original movies as they were intended. The Machete Order is intended to make the entire movies Luke centric but most of us clearly realize that Anakin is the true star of the movies and his story arc is what dominates the first six movies. And finally the reasoning that people would be confused by Hayden’s Anakin at the end of Return of the Jedi is over emphasized. Flic ignores the fact that there are non-special additions of the original trilogy that are still around and able to be seen. If you watch the original non-special additions that scene wouldn’t be confusing at all. And personally I loved Hayden’s Anakin’s Force Ghost. Sebastian Shaw was an unknown person and no one would automatically associate him with Anakin/Darth. Considering only other scene he appears in is covered in make up as Darth Vader’s face reveal in RoTJ. Sure watching the movies in their original theatrical release isn’t perfect storytelling but I much prefer it. Finally the Disney trilogy has no bearing on the original six movies which is why their order remains unchanged. I hope that clears up any confusion! Question: Can you explain how warp drive functions in the Star Wars universe?
Answer: There is no warp drive in Star Wars (you’re thinking of Star Trek) but there is hyperspace drive hyperspace There are some main differences between the two different modes of travel. Hyperspace is actually another dimension in Star Wars. When a vessel uses a hyperdrive, it enters the shadow dimension of Hyperspace which coexists simultaneously with regular space. Warp drive on the other hand creates a warp field that forms a subspace bubble that enveloped the starship. Warp drive also distorted the space time continium. Both traveling in hyperspace and using warp drive enable a vessel to travel faster than the speed of light. But Hyperspace drive or hyperdrive is infinitely faster than warp drive. In fact hyperdrive leaves warp drive in the dust. Hyperspace Traveling across the known Galaxy with hyperdrive takes about an afternoon, or a few days if your ship is slow. It would take a lifetime with a warp drive, as the Voyager found out. With a hyperdrive and enough fuel, Voyager could have made it home in time for tea with their afternoon coffee. Warp drive The whole plot of Voyager was that the ship was stranded in a remote sector of the galaxy and it would've taken it DECADES to crawl back. In Star Wars setting, even if you have a very crummy hyperdrive, same amount of travel at worst will take you a month or so. Warp drive Though warp drive does not require calculations to initiate travel. You can theoretically just point it at a direction and fire it off. The only way warp is better than hyperdrive is flexibility. Warp drive In Star Wars, you have to travel down set hyperlanes with near enough fixed entry and exit points. This is why combat is so close quarters in the vastness of space: fleets know where other fleets will come into and out of. However as I mentioned above, warp is much much slower. Eye of Sion In Ahsoka, we witnessed that with powerful enough engines and hyperdrive, one could even leave the known Galaxy. So in conclusion, Star Wars vehicles operate in hyperspace lanes rather than using Star Trek’s warp drive. And of course… I hope that clears up any confusion! Question: How did Anakin become a Force Ghost in Return of the Jedi?
Answer: Obi-Wan called out to Anakin after he passed away and taught him the ability to become a Force Spirit Fans have wondered for years how exactly Anakin was taught the ability to transcend death and become a Force Ghost. Finally this mystery was revealed in the short story, Brotherhood, from a Certain Point of View: Return of the Jedi. In the chapter “Brotherhood”, Anakin left his body of Vader and resided in the Living Force. However, instead of dispersing within the Force like most people, Anakin discovered that he kept his individuality, and consciousness actually grew stronger. For a time Anakin alternated between experiencing for the first time in his life true peace and for the first time fighting for his life, not because he wanted to live, but because he wanted to undo all the evil and suffering he had caused. As that happened Anakin heard the voices of his loved ones and finally he gave into the currents he was fighting. After giving in, Skywalker heard the voice of his old Master, Kenobi. Obi-Wan joked with Anakin telling him cause there was no Holonet for the poster boy anymore. Anakin respdonded sourly that he was no hero and then he had done terrible things and taken so many from so many people, including Obi-Wan himself. It was a watershed moment and Anakin began to confess all of his sins to his Old Master. Obi-Wan retorted that none of that mattered and a person is not completely made up of the choices that they make. Anakin responded that he wanted power to save others, but instead he destroyed them. Kenobi reassured Skywalker and told him that he did not make all of those those decisions on his own, and he doesn’t bear the guilt or sins of the galaxy, just his own. But Kenobi said he wanted his old Padawan to understand that the most important decision was the choice to chose life and goodness over death and darkness, that was the real choice and Anakin chose correctly. Kenobi then told Anakin he wanted to show him something. Kenobi transported them to the scene in RotJ, when Luke was burning his body and the party and celebration that followed. Anakin watched his children and their friends with happiness and a smile. Anakin mused on the thought that as a Padawan and a Knight he had always stood alone trying to solve everything for everyone and protect everyone. But he was never actually present in the moment with his loved ones as his children are right now. He realizes that all of his loved ones were always there urging him to let go of his attachments and be in the moment and he had never listened. His misguided beliefs of trying to be a ‘hero’, to be what he assumed others wanted him to be was always his ego. Letting go of attachments wasn’t as much as a physical thing as much as it was an acceptance of who he truly was and he had never considered that. Obi-Wan pointed out that the twins are what was best of who Anakin and Padme were. As Anakin accepted this he realized that he had manifested himself on the physical plane with Obi-Wan. Anakin then realized that he was wearing the Jedi robes a Jedi Master and became embarrassed. He told Obi-Wan it wasn’t intentional on his part, but Kenobi replied that Anakin might not have chosen it, but perhaps it chose him. Anakin then suddenly noticed that Luke was staring at him and could see him and then Anakin really looked at his daughter and realize how much she reminded him of Padme. Yoda suddenly appeared and told Anakin that his children had a hard and uncertain future road ahead of them. Anakin felt the urge (his ego) to try to step in and fix things, but this time he truly let it go. He simply told Yoda and Obi-Wan that he had faith in his children and for the first time ever, Anakin truly let go. That was the final lesson that Anakin had to learn, and he realized that that moment that it was of course, Obi-Wan that gave him the nudge in that direction . And if you wonder why Anakin appeared as his younger self, well that’s because the taint of Vader was gone once Anakin saved the Galaxy. Skywalker finally regained his loss humanity, and became the best version of himself which is when he was truly Anakin. I hope that clears up any confusion! Question: What weapons did Jedi and Sith use before lightsabers?
Answer: The Jedi and Sith used a variety of weapons before lightsabers during the first Jedi/Sith conflict, the Force Wars of Tython The earliest known conflicts between the Jedi and the Sith were called the Force Wars of Tython. The battles between the Jedi and Sith first took place on the planet Tython. The Force Wars were fought with primitive steel blades that were forged with the Force and were also enhanced and strengthened by the Force as well. The earliest Jedi even used the Force to sharpen their metal blades. The Force helped to sharpen and refine the blades finer than any non Force User could. Later Jedi began using the Force for even more refined techniques like for example, they used the Force to forge the blade themselves. These blades were forged by and known as Force imbued blades. These were solid metal blades that required no power source, and that glowed with the power of the Force coursing through them. They were made by an initiate who would select a bar of high carbon metal, typically durasteel (though other nigh unbreakable and durable steel would work just as well). As it was forged, the Force was channeled into the blade, altering the molecular structure of the metal into a reinforced lattice. Then the initiate would place a crystal into the hilt of the blade. The Force wielder would channel energy through the crystal and into the blade until it began to glow with a nimbus of energy, signifying that the blade had been permanently infused with the Force. Forcesaber The weapon of the Jedi and Sith would dramatically transform and change over the millennia's. The Force imbued Blades were the Jedi Order’s signature weapon until the introduction of the Forcesaber circa 25,793 BBY. Forcesaber The Forcesaber was a Rakatan invention in which dark side energy was channeled through a laboratory grown ebon crystals in glowing energy blades. The Forcesaber could be ignited like the much later developed lightsaber. the powerful Forcesaber Even though the Forcesaber was created with the Dark Side, it was used widely by the Sith, the Infinite Empire and the Je'daii (Jedi) Order. Because of its liberal use of the Dark Side, any Je’daii were at great risk of succumbing to the Darkside with each and every use of the Forcesaber. Forcesabers also came in a variety of colors. Xesh favored purple, Trill a light blue, and Lok wielded red after a force vision he saw. Kwa Master favored orange the same color the Rakatan used. The Flesh Raiders, mutated Rakata themselves, used yellow. Forcesaber The Je’daii Order would take the basic principles and technology of the Forcesaber and eventually developed their own weapon, the Protosaber. Protosaber This new weapon was created in about 7000 BBY and was the standard weapon of the Jedi by 5000 BBY. Protosabers, or Archaic lightsabers, were the first known design of a lightsaber. Photosabers, like later lightsabers, had a focusing crystal set inside a hilt from which a blade of energy was emitted. The main difference between protosabers and later lightsabers was that the hilt was connected via cable to an external power pack due to limitations in power pack technology. Protosabers are so popular that science geeks have tried in vain to make the world’s first working protosaber until now. Hacksmith has created a real 4000° Protosaber One Jedi did resurrect the Protosaber during the New Rupublic years, dubbing it the Retrosaber. Retrosaber A retrosaber was just as potent as modern lightsabers, but offered a few advantages along with the disadvantage of the external power pack. This was discussed in: Jedi Academy Training Manual The primary advantage was that modern belt-mounted power packs allowed for a brief "power surge", creating a more powerful blade for a short time and therefore a temporary advantage in combat. The Sith actually were the first invent a portable lightsaber much like the modern ones we are so accustomed to. The modern lightsaber is very similar to the Sith lightsaber because the modern was based on original Sith designs. The Sith design introduced an internal superconductor, which transferred the returning looped energy from the negative-charged flux aperture back into an internal power cell. With this modification, the power cell would only expend power when the energy loop was broken, such as when the lightsaber cut something, solving the power supply problem. Eventually the Jedi Order recognized the superiority of the Sith lightsaber over their own protosabers and the Order began to copy, mass produce and equip all Jedi with this version (albeit with a real kyber crystal unlike the Sith). So in conclusion, the Jedi and the Sith used a number of Force weapons before creating the lightsaber. I hope that clears up any confusion! I 💖C2, questions, disagreements, curses and hexes! -Jason

Question: Who invented the atom?
Answer: Democritus (420 BC-died 370 BC) was an ancient Socratic Greek philosopher who first formulated and postulated the theory of the atom and atomic theory in the Universe Democritus Democritus built upon the theories of his teacher Leucippus of Miletus who first conceived the theory of an atom. Democritus began to study and think about the make up atoms. Democritus grew up in a very wealthy and educated family. His father was very wealthy and had ties to Ancient Persia. He was said to have recieved Xerxes as his guest and entertained the God King and his vast army as Xerxes was passing through on his way back from overrunning and burning Athens and other city states who supported the Ionian rebellion. Xerxes was impressed with his host and in thanks left several Zoroastrian scholar priests Democritus himself believed that atoms were uniform, hard, incompressible and indestructible, and they moved throughout the infinite space until they were stopped. “Atoms and void being infinite in number and extent, and motion having always existed, there must always have been an infinite number of worlds, all consisting of similar atoms in various stages of growth and decay.” Source: Democritus Democritus Democritus also asserted: ”That space, or the Void, had an equal right with reality, or Being, to be considered existent. He conceived of the Void as a vacuum, an infinite space in which moved an infinite number of atoms that made up Being (i.e., the physical world).” “These atoms are eternal and indivisible; absolutely small, so small that their size cannot be diminished (hence the name atomon, or “indivisible”); absolutely full and incompressible, as they are without pores and entirely fill the space they occupy; and homogenous, differing only in shape, arrangement, position, and magnitude.” “But, while atoms thus differ in quantity, differences of quality are only apparent, owing to the impressions caused on the senses by different configurations and combinations of atoms.” Source: Democritus Interestingly enough Democritus wrote extensively on a wide variety of topics.Democritus wrote on ethics as well as physics. Question: Do you have any famous ancestors?
Answer: I do. Grace O’Malley, the famous Irish Pirate Queen, is one of my ancestors Grace O’Malley My mother’s maiden name is O’Malley and her family emigrated from Ireland in the 19th century. My uncle, before he passed did an ancestry site and looked up information on a genealogy site and found that Grace O’Malley was indeed a relative of mine. Grace O’Malley was born in 1530 in County Mayo, western Ireland. Grace was the daughter of the O'Malley chieftain, Owen 'Dubhdara' (Black Oak) O'Malley and Margaret O'Malley. County Mayo Ireland at this time did not have a King nor a centralized government but instead different parts of the land and counties were ruled by various clans and families. The O’Malleys lived off the coast of western Ireland, as I mentioned above, in the County of Mayo. Even before Grace was born, The O’Malleys had had a long history of piracy and making raids off of not only the Irish coast, but the Scottish coast and down to France as well. Grace O'Malley grew up at the family castles of Belclare and Clare Island. It’s likely that she would have been educated at the local monastery. Her father from a very young age took Grace with him on their ships as they did their piracy, raiding and trading. Being on the sea, was in Grace’s blood and she took to it better than her brother or any other Clansman under her father. She was eventually given control over the family’s ships and led raids herself because she was the better sailor and was more intelligent, more cunning and more gifted. This helped Grace garner the support of the sailors who served under her. It was virtually unheard of at the time for a woman to inherit the main title of a clan chief but Grace incredibly did just that. After her father died at a very young age, I believe she was 17, Grace took her place as the head of the O’Malley Clan and used all of the skills and the experience that her father taught her. “Like every accomplished mariner she had to know when it was safe to sail, and when it was safer to stay ashore,” biographer Anne Chambers explains. “She had to be in tune and respectful of that dangerous ocean.” Source: The extraordinary Life of Grace O’Malley Grace first took control of her father’s ships and head of the Clan. Grace and her fleet of ships took her as far north as Scotland plundering along the way, and as far south as Spain, taking cattle, riches and whatever she desired. At this time there was no currency in Ireland and everything that was bought and traded was weighed against the value of a cow. Grace and her clan had thousands of cows that she either traded for or absconded with during her raiding parties. Cock’s Castle renamed Hen’s Castle after Grace She also introduced a new type of piracy which was a toll for safe passage across the seas in which her Clan claimed. Meaning any ship that would pass by the western coast of Ireland near County Mayo would be stopped and would be forced to pay Grace’s tax. Even Phillip II of Spain agreed to pay the tax to Grace O’Malley for 20 years rather than try to fight her and her ships. “Grace and her clan took tolls on ships which she maintained were passing illegally through waters controlled by the O’Malley clan for generations.” Anne says. “It was a very busy route, with traffic coming up from Spain to the busy port of Galway and onwards to Ulster and Scotland.” Source: Supra Grace boasted a fleet that probably numbered from at least 10 to 20. Each ship could carry around 200 men. Her power was so great that even other men from other Clans deserted their families and went to work for Grace because she was such an accomplished pirate. Castle owned by Grace O’Malley She was married for a short time, but her first husband died fighting other clansman. When she was 20 years old, she married again for political reasons specifically because she wanted to capture and hold one specific castle. Under Gaelic law, both Irish men and women could divorce their partner after a year and a day. And exactly after a year and a day of her second marriage, Grace kicked her husband out of the castle and kept it. She remarried him for political reasons a couple of years later because she needed his support and arms. One of the most famous stories about her when she was pregnant with her fourth child, she was still serving as Captain of her large fleet of ships. Her Ships came into contact with Algerian pirates and a vicious fight ensued. Grace gave birth to her youngest son on board and after the baby was safely delivered, she took up arms and helped turn the tide and defeated the Algerian pirates. Stories like these just increased her fame and infamy. Her increasing power greatly alarmed England and the court of Queen Elizabeth I. A letter to the Tudor court described her as: “the nurse to all rebellions in the province for 40 years.” She plundered and conquered for almost 50 years. Eventually the English who had long wanted to bring Ireland under its control captured her youngest son. In a bid to free him, Grace did the unthinkable and requested an audience with Queen Elizabeth I at her court. Grace O’Malley and Queen Elizabeth I Amazingly, Elizabeth agreed and from all accounts from those who were at court, said that the two women spoke at length and seem to have found common ground. Grace deftly told Elizabeth, the trials and tribulations and how tough it was for her to serve as the clan chief and as a woman. As I mentioned above, it would seem that the two did find common ground because Elizabeth agreed to release her son and allowed Grace and her son to leave freely and return to their home. The English, over the many years of Grace’s life, took large swaths of land in Ireland and began to dominate the whole country. Grace aligned herself with England during the Nine Years War to ensure her Clan and her son would survive. Grace finally died the same year as Queen Elizabeth in 1603 at the age of 72. She had successfully been a pirate for over 40 years, which is longer than any other pirate that I ever remember studying. And unlike most of the other pirates, O’Malley actually lived to old age, and died peacefully still retaining much of her power. Grace was buried in Rockfleet Castle, Ireland. Grace O’Malley was an amazing pirate, a charismatic leader, and successfully navigated the treacherous world. Specifically the volatile time when war between England and Ireland dominated most of her life. She was an amazing woman, and I’m happy and honored to call her my ancestor. I hope that clears up any confusion! I 💖C2, questions, disagreements, curses and hexes! -Jason

Question: If you wanted to rank all the people who took the super soldier serum in the MCU, who is the strongest?
Answer: Well, I do think there are differences in each Super Soldier Serum and how effective it was on its host but physical strength was not the barometer to test how successful or effective the serum was The most successful Super Soldier Serums imparted on its user the most advanced physiological capabilities but at the time kept its user’s sanity and didn’t warp or distort their personality or emotional state. 1.Abraham Erskine's Super Soldier Serum The most successful and most powerful recipient of the Super Soldier Serum was of Steve Rogers. "The strong man who has known power all his life may lose respect for that power, but a weak man knows the value of strength, and knows compassion." Erskine's super soldier serum had to be used in combination with vita radiation in order to have safe and stable effects, so Steve Rogers was simultaneously injected with the serum and bombarded with the Vita Rays. Vita Radiation is electromagnetic radiation with a specific wavelength that has stabilizing properties. It was used to activate the properties of the Super Soldier Serum in Steve. The Vita-Rays increased Rogers muscularity and his height. They also had the ability to enhance whatever was on the inside. Good or evil. Rogers kept his altruistic kind hearted courageous nature even after transforming into Captain America. He also began to age considerably slower and slower than most of the other recipients, except for a few. 2. Arnim Zola's Super Soldier Serum After Erskine escaped and began developing his Super Soldier Serum for the United States instead, scientist Arnim Zola took over the job of trying to perfect HYDRA's version. Even though Zola lacked access to Vita-Rays, he still managed to create an almost identical Serum to Erskine’s version. Bucky was mentally broken by Hydra but it wasn’t Zola’s Serum that permanently disfigured him mentally and physically like what happened to Johann. He used captured American soldiers as test subjects for his experimentation with the super soldier serum, and one of these test subjects was Bucky Barnes. After being exposed to the Serum, HYDRA tortured Barnes and used a combination of cybernetics and brainwashing to transform him into the Winter Soldier. Even though HYDRA’s violent manipulations, Barnes true personality and goodness survived. And Zola’s Serum did not alter Bucky’s personality either. Shuri got ahold of Zola’s Winter Soldier notes when Arnim was in USSR custody in the 1940s. "My work continues in secret. In the cold desolation of Siberia, the next Hydra soldier is being born. Finally, Barnes ages considerably more slowly about the same rate as Steve Rogers himself. Bucky proved time and time again to be Steve Rodgers’ equal. 3. Alexei Alanovich Shostakov aka Red Guardian Alexei was born in the Soviet Union in the mid/late 20th century. Shostakov joined the Soviet Armed Forces and was chosen to become the Soviet Union’s first Super Soldier to counteract Captain America. The Soviet Union’s Red Room scientists based their Serum on Zola and Hydra’s work. The Red Guardian gained all the powers and abilities of Captain America and the Winter Soldier. And thankfully Alexei, also did not have any of the mind or emotional altering effects that some of the other recipients experienced (The Red Skull). The Soviet Scientists also found a way to perfect the Serum without the use of Vita-Rays as well. I surmise that the Red Room also exposed Shostakov to gamma radiation as a way of mimicking the Vita-Rays. The Soviet Serum was just as successful as Arnim’s and Erskine’s and Alexei’s personality did not alter and he stayed the same fun, loving and lighthearted person that he always was. Red Guardian was just as powerful as Captain America and the Winter Soldier and aged just as slowly as they did. 4. Isaiah Bradley's Super Soldier Serum After the death of Abraham Erskine and the later disappearance of Captain America, the United States began trying to recreate the Super Soldier Serum and used Black soldiers as test subjects. In the limited comic book series Truth: Red, White and Black (upon which The Falcon and the Winter Soldier is partly based), these new versions of the serum frequently resulted in horrifying deaths for the men who received them. Bradley was one of the few test subjects for whom the serum worked, and the only super soldier who ultimately survived. Bradley became the new Captain America and by all accounts had the equivalent abilities to Captain America and Isaiah also kept his own good and moral personality. He was Captain America inside and out. Bradley was even sent to the war in Korea to hunt down and kill the Winter Soldier but was only successful in tearing off Bucky's arm. 5. The Red Skull's Super Soldier Serum Erskine first began working on the super soldier serum in 1930, and when the Nazis came into power both they and HYDRA forced him to continue developing his formula for their purposes. Schmidt took Erskine’s formula, but without the stabilizing effect of Vita radiation the serum caused the skin on Schmidt's face to burn and turn red, earning him his supervillain moniker: the Red Skull. Despite this unfortunate side effect, Erskine said that the serum did not fail, but did exactly what it was designed to do. Just as the serum would later amplify Steve Rogers' goodness, bravery and compassion, it amplified Johann Schmidt's evil and lust for power. He magnified all the power and evil that already exisfed within Johann. 6. Dr. Wilfred Nagel's Super Soldier Serum The Falcon and the Winter Soldier introduces the latest iteration of the super soldier serum, this time developed by scientist Dr. Wilfred Nagel and reverse-engineered from Isaiah Bradley's blood. Flag Smasher vs Bucky Nagel first worked for HYDRA, then for the CIA, and then finally for the Power Broker in Madripoor while developing his super soldier serum, which he believed to be superior to Erskine's. The serum doesn't require vita radiation to be stabilized, and doesn't physically change the appearance of the recipient's body. However, it does still appear to have the affect of enhancing a person's fundamental personality for better or worse. Or for John Walker in particular, I think the serum tempted him into tapping into his darker side. Though whether that's a physical effect or a psychological response to suddenly having great power is uncertain. 7. Howard Stark's Super Soldier Serum In 1991 a new version of the super soldier serum was developed by Iron Man's father, Howard Stark. Before it could be used on any American test subjects, however, Howard was murdered by the Winter Soldier and the five doses of his Super Soldier Serum were delivered to HYDRA. The serum was given to HYDRA's elite death squad, who had "more kills than anyone in HYDRA's history," according to Bucky. This attempt to create more Winter Soldiers was deemed a failure, and the test subjects were put on ice in HYDRA's Siberia facility until they were eventually killed by Zemo. 8. General Ross recruited scientist Bruce Banner to recreate Erskine's formula, and Banner developed a new serum that was used in combination with gamma radiation instead of vita radiation. Unfortunately this proved to be anything but stable, transforming Banner into a giant green rage monster who became known as the Incredible Hulk. Rather than enhancing his personality, as the previous versions of the super soldier serum had, Banner's formula had the effect of splitting his personality between the mild-mannered Bruce and the ill-mannered Hulk. 9. Emil Blonsky's Super Soldier Serum Thaddeus Ross didn't give up on the super soldier serum even after the Hulk nearly killed him and his daughter. His new version of Project Rebirth continued working on serums until he found one that was "very promising." This was offered to Captain Emil Blonsky at a very low dose, and seemed to have the desired effect of enhancing speed, strength and agility without any negative side effects. Unfortunately for Blonsky, he wasn't yet strong enough to beat the Incredible Hulk. After he healed from having most of the bones in his body shattered, Blonsky was given a larger dose of the new serum that began to mutate his body and unravel his mind. Now lusting for power to match the Incredible Hulk, Blonsky injected himself with Bruce Banner's gamma-irradiated blood and transformed into the Abomination. I list Blonsky’s version as the lowest because of the extreme physical transformations that he went through that are irreversible. Though it does seem that he found a level of peace and tranquility as we saw in the She Hulk. I hope that clears up any confusion! I 💖C2, questions, disagreements, curses and hexes! -Jason

Question: Where was Troy during the battle of Thermopylae? Did they join afterwards? Who was King of Troy during this time?

Troy of Homer’s tales fell a thousand years before the time of the Battle of Thermopylae. At the time of the Trojan War, Troy’s population was probably around 10,000 and Troy’s own forces combined with hired mercenaries, bolstered their numbers to about 10,000–12,000 strong. The Trojans during this time period were also allies of the mighty Hittite Empire (Troy was called Wilusa by the Hittites). There is some evidence that the treaty between the two nations promised troop support to each other. It is believed the Hittites offered troops who fought with the Trojans against the Greeks (and there is some evidence that Trojans joined the Hittites against Egypt at the Battle of Kadesh). Troy VI of the Late Bronze Age and Trojan War The Hittites probably bolstered the Trojan ranks with another 5,000–7,000. Troy was rich and prosperous through its many years of trade and its control over the waterways. Troy VI in the Late Bronze Age The city could afford not only the best training and weapons for their own troops, but also the high prices of mercenaries as well. They could also reimburse the Hittite Empire. Trojans on their mighty walls Troy was a city that had existed for thousand of years and the Troy of the Trojan War is designated Troy VI. Troy VI (1750–1300 B.C.). was the most monumental of Troy's prehistoric settlements, surpassing all previous settlements in its size and scope. Troy VI It represents a time when the city flourished, the population grew, industry thrived, and grandiose houses were built. The inhabited citadel, which was surrounded by towering walls, grew to occupy a space covering 5 acres, at least twice the size of previous cities. Troy VI’s giant walls Troy VI is often connected with the Homeric tradition, the Trojan War, and the city of Wilusa that is mentioned in contemporary Hittite. Troy VI Troy had been built and and been destroyed countless times. Troy VI as I mentioned probably had 10,000–15,000 citizens. By the time of 480 B.C., a new city exists on the remains of Troy called Ilion. During the first few centuries after the Battle of Thermopylae, Ilion was a modest settlement, although it later grew thanks to its association with Homer's works. It was a settlement of about 1,500 -2,000 inhabitants and the new settlers chose the area because if was the setting of the Trojan War. The Inhabitants took advantage of this to draw in political support and ancient tourists. They had no King by this time period. By the time Archaic Age, a thousand years after Troy VI’s destruction and long after the time of Homer, the great and the powerful visited the site to pay homage to the heroes of old. Xerxes, the Persian king (lived 519-466 B.C.), stopped to pay homage to Troy on his way to attack Greece around 480 B.C. Ironically Xerxes visited Ilion on way his to annihilate the Spartans. Xerxes visited Illion Illion had no warriors and their only source of income was from visitors. They had no intention of hurting one of their richest visitors of all time, Xerxes, the God King himself. Xerxes Alexander the Great in ancient Troy Alexander the Great (356 to 323 B.C.) did the same on his way to conquer the Persian Empire, where he apparently dedicated his armour to the Trojan Athena. Alexander pays homage to Athena at Illion Alexander took from her shrine ancient arms and a shield which had been preserved from the Trojan War. Finally, Julius Caesar visited the ruins of Troy in 48 B.C. Cesar in Illion Constantine the Great tried to found his capital here in the 4th century AD before choosing Byzantium (Istanbul) instead. Troy's harbour had silted up and was no longer suitable. Constantine the Great Sadly Ilion was a mere village from the Archaic Age to the birth of Christ. They hardly had any soldiers to give or loan to the Spartans during the Battle of Thermopylae. Constantine the Great The Romans, of course, traced their ancestry back to Troy, believing that their city was founded by the Trojan prince Aeneas who managed to escape the final destruction. Early medieval dynasties also used this story as their founding legend. I hope that clears up any confusion! i 💖C2, questions, disagreements, curses and hexes! -Jason

Question: Who is the first woman who won an Olympic title?

Question: What archeological evidence is there for the existence of a historical civilization like Atlantis, Lemuria, or Mu?
Answer: Very little if any evidence exists at all proving the existence of Lemuria, Mu or Atlantis First let’s start with Lemuria. Lemuria was first introduced by Philip Lutley Sclater, an English zoologist in 1864. Lemuria was born out of a conundrum that perplexed Sclater. Lemurs Sclater was studying Lemurs and couldn’t understand why fossil records of Lemurs in Madagascar and the Indian Subcontinent were so similar but Lemurs in continental Africa and the Middle East were very much different. Philip Lutley Sclater The only way he could make sense of this weird fossil record is if there was a land bridge or continent that connected Madagascar to the Indian subcontinent. I remember learning that when he first postulated Lemuria it was sort of as a joke because it was an easy way to understand and fix his fossil Conundrum. He thought that possibly a now submerged continent used to exist in the Indian Ocean. Over the years, many people co opted the theory of Lemuria to fit their own agenda. Originally the biologist, eugenicist and racist Ernst Haeckel theorized that Lemuria was the lost continent where Homo sapiens came from. Haeckel’s theory was preposterous and later disproven. Ernst Haeckel, racist, eugenicist and all around not a good guy Over the years, occultists, mystics and other lunatics co opted Lemuria for themselves. The occult leader of the Theosophical Society, Helena Blavatsky, taught that Lemuria was the ancestral homeland of humans which she called Lemurians. Lemurians She made this ridiculous claim in the late 19th century, but other mystics and a cult leaders picked up her ideas and built upon them. Helena Blavatsky, occultist and lunatic If you’re familiar with Mount Shasta in Northern California, then you’re probably aware and heard of the secret society of Lumerians supposedly escaped their submerged continent in the Pacific Ocean. This is all bogus and untrue. Lemuria, ridiculous and untrue Mu is another lost continent and lost civilization originally created by Augustus Le Plongeon who associated Mu with Atlantis and later Lemuria as well in the late 19th century as well. Plongeon thought that Lemuria or Mu was a submerged continent in the Pacific Ocean. He had no proof to prove his theory yet pushed it nonetheless. Mu The theory of continental drift, first theorized by Alfred Wegene, a climatologist and geologist, in 1912 was proven true in the 1960s. Continental drift is the theory that Earth’s continents float and crash into each other over time. Continental drift was later adopted under the name of plate tectonics. Continental Drift Wegener even figured out which continents might be submerged and theorized as well that all the continents at one time were connected as a supercontinent. Alfred Wegener Wegener’s theories, later proven true, specifically stated that there were no lost continents where humans originated because there simply had not been enough time past in geological terms to account for any lost continents being submerged. Plate tectonics over the last 200 million years Any continents (and the plates they sit upon) if submerged would have happened millions of years ago and not recent enough to account for human beings. This of course, was lost on all the mystics and occultists who still pushed their outlandish crackpot theories. Atlantis Atlantis as well could not have existed as a lost civilization and continent because there hasn’t been enough time past to account for a continent being submerged and lost. Atlantis I left Atlantis till the end because I do believe that the story of Atlantis was based upon the lost island of Thera or known today as Santorini. I think the eruption of Thera, a violent volcanic explosion that destroyed some of the islands of Santorini, was the basis for the legend of Atlantis. Eruption of Thera The eruption of Thera crippled the Minoan civilization and hastened its demise near the end of the Bronze Age. The eruption took place around 1600 B.C. Plato And Plato was born in 427 B.C., a thousand years after the eruption. Plato offered no proof of the existence of Atlantis but he was told the legend and tale of Atlantis passed on through Countless generations. When he was young Plato was regaled stories of Atlantis from his mother. Santorini after the eruption The Minoan civilization predated the Greeks of Plato’s time by a thousand years. The Minoan civilization was incredibly advanced, especially for its time. The Minoans were a peaceful society who built its wealth and prestige through trade rather than war. Minoan Frescoes The Minoans were incredibly advanced in so many areas. Their sophisticated art included elaborate seals, pottery (especially the famous Kamáres ware with its light-on-dark style of decoration), and, above all, delicate, vibrant frescoes found on palace walls. Minoan Frescoes These frescoes display both secular and religious scenes, such as magical gardens, monkeys, and wild goats or fancifully dressed goddesses that testify to the Minoans’ predominantly matriarchal religion. Minoan Snake Goddess The Minoans most likely had slaves, but didn’t rely on them like many of the contemporary civilizations and later ones. Likewise, they did not have slaves in the thousands the way other empires were built upon them. The Minoans did not kill their animals for sport but used them in acrobatic acts and others like it. Minoan game The ancient Minoans also had running water, an incredibly advanced sewage system and may even have had an early form of a shower. Their early plumbers had laid elaborate systems of sewage disposal and drainage that resemble one of today. Minoan Sewer System They are cited as being the first civilization to use underground plumbing for washing and bathrooms with a dedicated sewer system. This shows how people from the Minoan civilization maintained their personal hygiene. Minoan Civilization The Minoans captivated later civilizations including the Myceanans and other later, Greek cultures. I’m sure stories of how advanced the Minoan civilization was would make any Greek during Plato‘s time seem like it was a paradise on Earth. I personally think that Plato himself heard tales about the ancient Minoans but those stories over time had been transformed into the mythical Atlantis. So I conclusion, Mu and Lemuria are completely made up, but the theory of Atlantis may have been based upon real historical facts and a real civilization. I hope that clears up any confusion! Lucasfilm's The Art of The Mandalorian, features a fascinating discourse from Filoni on the subject of balance. He explores the nature of the light and dark sides of the Force, and the role every person in the galaxy must play in order to sustain balance. The dark side of the Force is manifested in our greed, desire for power, and fears.” “And the light side of the Force is propagated by selfless action, by living in balance, by overcoming our fears. It is a critical choice and one that greatly impacts both their lives." -Dave Filoni Finally, George Lucas built upon the Jedi’s view of balance, and said this: “Many fans incorrectly assume that balance refers to an equal mix of both light and dark side users. However, as George Lucas explains in the introductory documentary for the VHS version A New Hope, Special Edition, this is not the case:” "[...] Which brings us up to the films 4, 5, and 6, in which Anakin's offspring redeem him and allow him to fulfill the prophecy where he brings balance to the Force by doing away with the Sith and getting rid of evil in the universe..." In an interview, Lucas compared the difference between the light and dark sides as being like the difference between a symbiotic relationship and a cancer. “A symbiotic relationship is one which benefits both parties and in which neither is harmed, whereas a cancer takes without giving back, eventually causing the death of both parties.” -George Lucas Kenobi misunderstood the Chosen One Prophecy The Jedi never wanted to destroy the Dark Side, just contain it. Question: In Star Trek canon why was "1701" chosen for the Enterprise registry number?
Answer: The 17 stood for the fact that the Constitution-class was Starfleet’s 17th starship design and that the Enterprise was the first, 01, Constitution Class to be constructed producing its number 1701 The USS Constitution was the prototype, therefore its designation was NCC-1700. Since it was the first Constitution Class starship, its registry number was 0, hence the 1700. The U.S.S. Enterprise was the first produced Constitution Class starship built after the original and therefore had the registry number 1701. In canon I don’t think there was ever an explanation what NCC stood for. Matt Jefferies, the artist and set designer for the original series, gave a much more practical and mundane reason for the 1701 designation. “The one seven zero part - I needed a number that would be instantly identifiable, and three, six, eight and nine are too easily confused. I don’t think anyone’ll confuse a one and a seven, or the zero.” -Matt Jefferies Matt Jefferies 1701 was also chosen because the numbers were quite distinctive and looked good on the Enterprise’s hull. Eventually, NCC became the prefix for standard ships. NX is the prefix for experimental ships. 1701 became the official Enterprise registry number. Any other Federation Enterprises inherit that number, but with a letter suffix to differentiate. For example, the Enterprise Picard has in TNG is the NCC 1701-D. Question: What are some amazing and interesting historical facts or theories that are little known?
Answer: I’ve got a couple of interesting historical facts Just Joshing You 5 cent Liberty Head You may have heard the phrase “Just Joshing You.” What you might not actually know is the interesting history behind the phrase. Josh Tatum, was a deaf mute career criminal from Boston. 1883 $5 Gold Coin In 1883, the United States released a new 5 cent nickel called the Liberty Head or V nickel. Tatum noticed a glaring problem with the new 5 cent nickel. It looked quite similar to the $5 coin that had been in circulation, and on the back of the five cent nickel, it was missing the cents sign. 1883 $5 Gold Coin Tatum came up with a brilliant scheme and got an unscrupulous jeweler to help him by gold plating 1,000 of the new V nickels. Tatum then went to small stores and passed off the fake nickels as $5 pieces. He purchased small items usually costing 5 cents at these stores and took the change. The scam worked like a charm. Tatum commissioned his jeweler friend to gold plate thousands of more and he worked his way up and down the East Coast eventually making $15,000. Tatum was eventually arrested by the Secret Service and put on trial. In a funny twist of fate, Tatum’s attorney actually convince a jury to find him not guilty. His attorney argued that since Josh was mute and never spoke to any employee, he didn’t intend to scam the businesses. If Tatum received more change than he was due, his attorney argued that he just assumed this was a gift and accepted it. Naturally, the US mint quickly changed the design of their nickel and put the five cent mark on it to stop the problem, but quite an interesting story. But the term “Just Joshing You” came about as a result of this whole entertaining affair. It of course, just means you are joking with someone. Uncle Sam Most people recognize the fictional character Uncle Sam but most people don’t know the origin of the original name, and who it was based upon. Samuel Wilson Samuel Wilson was a business man from Troy, New York. During the War of 1812, Wilson being a true patriot wanted to help the war effort. He began to supply the United States military with beef, a desperately needed commodity. Wilson’s beef was transported in barrels marked with the initials “U.S.” But when people asked Wilson’s workers what the U.S. stood for they always responded Uncle Sam Wilson. Wilson was well known and respected and was known as Uncle Sam. There was a requirement at the time for contractors to stamp their name and where the rations came from onto the food they were sending. The suggestion that the meat came from Uncle Sam led to the belief that Uncle Sam symbolized the US federal government. Cartoonist of the day took advantage of this confusion, and began to draw pictures of a fictional Uncle Sam as the representative of the U.S. government. The most famous representation of Uncle Sam was created by James Montgomery Flagg in 1917 as an army recruiting symbol. Flagg used a mirror and his own likeness to create the iconic Uncle Sam image. And in 1961, Kennedy sponsored a resolution that was passed by Congress finally recognizing Sam Wilson as the inspiration for the symbol of Uncle Sam. I hope that clears up any confusion! Question: Why were the Moai statues built?
Answer: The Moai statues on Rapa Nui (Easter Island) served a number of purposes but their location and size indicated the presence of fresh water The inhabitants of Rapa Nui built the Moai as a way to honor and represent their ancestors. But much of what we thought we knew about the Moai and the people who built them has changed. Rapa Nui or Easter Island was discovered by Dutch explorers In 1722. The inhabitants of Rapa Nui first arrived on the island’s shores between 1150 and 1280 A.D. They lived in isolation until 1722. Scientists and archaeologists have long wondered how the people of Rapa Nui chose the locations where their Moai statues were built. Scientists have also long wondered how the people of Rapa Nui could have survived since Easter island gets little to no rainfall and and has no above ground streams or rivers flowing across it. And yet the inhabitants of Easter Island thrived for hundred of years and the community grew to its largest consisting of 10,000 people at its zenith. The location of fresh water had been a mystery for hundreds of years until recently. Researchers began to look at the locations of the ahu (the flat mounds) that the Moai were built upon for any possible water sources. Scientists with satellite technology discovered drinkable but brackish freshwater flowed out of the ground near the coast at low tide. After close inspection, they found that the many Moai were located and guarding the places near the coast where freshwater was available. The Moai marked the location of the few but vital freshwater sources. “Here, we use spatially-explicit point-process modeling to explore the potential relations between ahu construction locations and subsistence resources, namely, rock mulch agricultural gardens, marine resources, and freshwater sources—the three most critical resources on Rapa Nui. Through these analyses, we demonstrate the central importance of coastal freshwater seeps for precontact populations.” “Our results suggest that ahu locations are most parsimoniously explained by distance from freshwater sources, in particular coastal seeps, with important implications for community formation and inter-community competition in precontact times.” Source: Rapa Nui (Easter Island) monument (ahu) locations explained by freshwater sources The team found that rainwater at Easter Island sinks directly through porous bedrock into an underground aquifer (a body of porous rock or sediment where water is concentrated). Wherever the scientific team found water seeping out of the coast, they found platforms for statues. And even in areas in the interior where there were platforms but didn't seem to be any water, they found the remains of ancient wells that tapped the islands underground aquifers. Coastal Seep behind Ahu Tongariki This then surfaces along the coastline as something known as coastal seeps, pockets of freshwater that trickle into the ocean. The scientific team found that in addition to harvesting freshwater from pockets of coastal seep, Rapa Nui’s inhabitants built underwater dams in the ocean to keep fresh and seawater separated and constructed wells that redirected water from the aquifer before reaching the sea. The team also found that the size of the statues seemed to correspond to the amount of the water that was available. In areas completely devoid of freshwater resources, there were no moai or ahu. “Every time we saw massive amounts of fresh water, we saw giant statues,” co-author Carl Lipo from Binghamton University tells Davis. “It was ridiculously predictable.” Source: Easter Island statues marked fresh water supplies This recent study also contradicted the long-held belief that inhabitants of Rapa Nui suffered an ecological collapse as the different warring tribes scrambled for resources. Traditionally, scientists incorrectly believed that competition for resources led to warfare between the various tribes that lived on the island and the competition to build larger statues lead to the society’s eventual collapse. Instead, this new study discovered that the inhabitants and various tribes were cooperative with each other both in the construction of the Moai and in sharing resources most importantly water. Answer: In Canon and Legends, training children in the way of the Sith was both encouraged and prohibited depending upon which Sith organization was in charge Maul, for example in Canon, was stolen by Sidious at a young age from his Mother Talzin and trained in the ways of the Sith. “Sidious promised to make me his right hand, but instead, he stole what was most dear to me... my own flesh and blood. -Mother Talzin discussing her son Maul and Sidious Mother Talzin and her son Maul In Canon, Maul was taken by Sidious and beaten daily by two Nightbrothers chosen by Sidious. Maul was abused so badly daily, he could barely stand. Anger and rage festered in Maul just as Sidious had planned and wanted. In Legends, during Maul’s first year of birth, his Morher Talzin, persuaded Darth Sidious to take her son and train him in the ways of the Darkside. Maul was taken to Mustafar and trained by droids vigorously and savagely. Sith Academy In Legends, during some time periods Initiates were taken as children and trained in the ways of the Sith in institutions. But during other times, the Sith frowned upon training the very young, preferring to take an Apprentice, when they are older and more powerful in the Force. Sith Empire During the time of the Sith Empire, Force sensitive children were forcibly taken from their parents, and placed in Sith academic institutions. Darth Bane Darth Bane changed all that when he instituted the Rule of Two. Bane taught and preferred taking Apprentices that were older and not children. The Legends book, Darth Plagueis explained the rationale and reasoning why under the Rule of Two, Sith Apprentices were not chosen from children. “For the past five hundred years, the Sith of the Bane line had eschewed selecting children as apprentices, finding it more advantageous to discover beings who had already been hardened or scarred by life.” Darth Bane’s Apprentice Darth Zannah Darth Bane and those that followed preferred Sith Apprentices who had been scarred and beaten down by life before taking them as Apprentices. The Sith Empire instead preferred to fester that anger and hatred themselves by making their child Initiates suffer by their own hands. It is understandable why Bane changed the age when Apprentices were taken. The Rule of Two was based upon two full fledged Sith, one who has the power and one who craves it. To train an Apprentice to desire to overthrow their Master required an Apprentice that possessed the maturity and the power to do such an act. The Rule of Two was also based upon secrecy and subterfuge. Imperial Army of the Sith Empire During the time of the Sith Empire, the Sith was more like a military order and needed the large number of Sith shock troops to wage their wars across the galaxy. This required training from a very early age by a large number of Force sensitive children. Though in Legends, other Sith Lords broke this rule and trained their Apprentices from childhood. Darth Tenebrous convinced Hego Damask II’s parents to allow him to take their child and train him in the ways of Sith. Hego would eventually become Darth Plageuis. Darth Tenebrous and Darth Plageuis Plageuis in turn convinced a boy named Palpatine and convinced the latter to kill his family. Once that was done, Plageuis took Palpatine as a child as his Apprentice. So in conclusion, during some time periods, Sith were trained as children, and during other time periods, it was strictly forbidden, though the rule was often broken. I hope that clears up any confusion! I 💖C2, questions, disagreements, curses and hexes! -Jason

Question: Will Finn and Rey finally get together romantically in Rey Skywalker’s new movie?
Answer: Highly unlikely Very unlikely Kathleen Kennedy appeared at the Star Wars celebration to announce a new Star Wars film starring Daisy Ridley. Not much is known about the new film except that the previous writer Damon Lindelof was recently fired by Disney as well as Lindelof’s co writer Justin Britt-Gibson. They were both replaced by writer Steven Knight, best known in recent years as the creator of “Peaky Blinders.” Ms. Marvel” director Sharmeen Obaid-Chinoy has signed on to direct the new movie. The movie is confirmed to pick up after the events of Episode IX, effectively functioning as a sequel to The Rise of Skywalker. Kathleen Kennedy confirmed that the film will introduce an all-new era of the Star Warstimeline, officially titled "The New Jedi Order." The film purportedly takes place 10 years after the end of TRoS and introduces two new Jedi, a male and female that Rey is training. Of course, there have been rumors swirling as to whether John Boyega’s Finn or Oscar Isaac’s Poe Dameron will make their return in this film as well. A couple of years ago, both actors expressed their dissatisfaction with the Disney trilogy, its process and specifically in Boyega’s case, the sidelining of his character. Just friends In 2020, Boyega vented his frustrations, “You get yourself involved in projects and you’re not necessarily going to like everything,” he said. “[But] what I would say to Disney is do not bring out a black character, market them to be much more important in the franchise than they are and then have them pushed to the side. It’s not good. I’ll say it straight up.” “When it came to Kelly Marie Tran, when it came to John Boyega, you know f*ck all,” he added. “So what do you want me to say? What they want you to say is, ‘I enjoyed being a part of it. It was a great experience…’ Nah, nah, nah. I’ll take that deal when it’s a great experience. They gave all the nuance to Adam Driver, all the nuance to Daisy Ridley. Let’s be honest. Daisy knows this. Adam knows this. Everybody knows. I’m not exposing anything.” Source: Boyega very dissatisfied with Trilogy But his stance has changed as of late. When asked in July of 2023, John seems open to returning to Star Wars, “That was a few years ago, so they were the subject of that particular project,” Boyega told TechRadar about his comments. “But I’m open to all characters and scripts that are enjoyable, have a great cast attached and a terrific director. So yeah, I’m open to all opportunities.” Source: Supra Oscar originally stated he would not return to Star Wars, “Isaac couldn’t have been more blunt at the 2021 Venice Film Festival when he said, “I’ve been in green-screen space land for quite a few years and I was desperate to do a character study.” “It’s not really what I set out to do,” Isaac said in one interview about making “Star Wars”-sized movies. “What I set out to do was to make handmade movies, and to work with people that inspire me… It feels like for me a personal turning point and that, as far as I’m concerned, it has nothing to do with the finished product. It’s the process of doing this.” “Isaac famously joked in 2020 that he would only return to “Star Wars” for money and if “I need another house or something.” Source: Isaac burnt out from SW But as of late, Oscar has also changed his tune, “However, Isaac recently said during a SiriusXM interview that he’s “so open” to more “Star Wars” as long as “there was a great story and a great director.” “I don’t know. I’m open to anything. You never know,” Isaac said when asked about returning to the “Star Wars” franchise. “I have no real feeling one way or another. I’m open to any good story. Time is the one thing that becomes challenging…as you get older and kids and all that. Where do [movies] fit in? If there was a great story and a great director and [Lucasfilm president] Kathy [Kennedy] came to me and was like, ‘I have this great idea,’ then I’m so open to it.” Source: Supra So it would seem if the right script, and role for the characters made sense to both actors, John Boyega and Oscar Isaac are at least open fo the idea. That being said, it seems highly unlikely Rey and Finn will be ever be involved romantically. Rey’s character in the trilogy seemed to be almost asexual without any romantic interest except Adam Driver’s Kylo Ren. And in the orginal script for Episode IX, Duel of Fates, Poe and Rey enter into a romantic relationship. Poe and Rey in Love Unlike Rise of Skywalker, the script for Duel of the Fates did not sideline Rose and completely honored her relationship with Finn. Their romance was fully explored. Finn and Rose End Up Together The awkward Rey-Finn tension doesn't exist in Duel of the Fates, because Poe and Rey are off doing their own thing. While not everyone needs to be paired off, preserving the Finn and Rose pairing would have been a good thing. In Duel of the Fates, Poe Dameron’s character is respectful and does his best to not interfere with her Jedi training. He's supportive and very clearly learned some lessons from The Last Jedi. As far as Han Solo-types go, he's actually not a scoundrel. Whst Could’ve Been: the Happy Couple At one point during Duel of the Fates, Leia notices Rey is withholding her feelings for Poe because she's afraid of violating the Jedi code. Similarly, Anakin was told he couldn't get married and have kids, but he did it anyway and kept it a secret, which is partially why he became Darth Vader. The Kiss Many Wanted to See What's different here is that Leia calls out the Jedi teachings for being oppressive as hell. Rey tells Leia she can't follow her feelings for Poe because of the "rules," to which the general responds, "Written by whom? Some old man a thousand years before you were born." Roe- Rey and Poe marry and have a couple of kIds A vague trace of this idea survived in The Rise of Skywalker, when Leia tells Rey to "never be afraid of who you are." But since Rey's identity is all over the place in Rise of Skywalker, it doesn't really have the same punch. Rey and Poe in Love Now there is no indication that Daisy’s new Star Wars will retain any of the romance written into Duel of Fates with Poe. And it seems highly unlikely considering where Poe and Rey ended up by the end of TRoS. Poe was conveniently reunited with Zorii Bliss, a past romance and possible future one as well. In much the same way, I find it very difficult to believe that if Finn returns there will be any romance between him and Rey either. Finn seemed to be romantically involved with Rose and if not her then possibly Jannah played by Naomi Ackie. In fact, John Boyega on his twitter account, and Naomi Ackie in an interview, confirmed that Finn and Jannah have a romantic interest in each other in Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker. Ackie said, “One thing she can comfortably talk about is Jannah’s bond with Finn, which might come across as romantic to plenty of viewers. That’s the intent, Ackie says.” Source: Ackie opens up about Jannah Of course, the writer of the new movie could change all these relationships but I think it’s still very unlikely Finn will appear in the new movie and even if he did, even more unlikely that there will be any romantic connection with Rey and Finn. Rey will be too busy rebuilding the Jedi Order Disney has seemed relunctant to bring any real on screen romance with their main characters, as evidenced by their trilogy, and I don’t see that changing anytime soon. Just friends… So it looks like for the foreseeable future there will be no romance for Rey with Finn or Poe. I hope that clears up any confusion! Question: Is Darth Vader more powerful than Darth Sidious in the current Canon?

Consequently, Vader is the most powerful Sith Lord even surpassing even his Master. Let’s not forgot Vader did kill the Emperor and restored the Balance in the Force Two canon Disney/Lucasfilms properties specifically state that Darth Vader is the most powerful Sith Lord. The Video Game Jedi: Fallen Order is a canon source. It specifically states: “Few survive an encounter with the Most Powerful Sith Lord.” Jedi Fallen Order Also The Force Awakens Visual Dictionary states: “Through his veins courses the bloodline of the most powerful Jedi and Sith, and Ren sees it as his birthright to rule the weaker beings in the galaxy.” The Dark Lord of the Sith, in canon, did not lose any of his power or potential as the Chosen One after his injuries on Mustafar. Most people have a clear misunderstanding of how Midi-Chlorians work in the Star Wars Universe. Midi-Chlorians (MC) exist in every cell in every being that exists in the Star Wars universe. The MC count is the number of them inside each cell. Vader toyed with Reva and used only the Force to best her Even when Vader lost his limbs and much of his body, his MC count did not decline nor did his power and strength in the Force. Remember Luke doing this? He crushed the Death Trooper with his metallic hand proving the use of the Force is unaffected by the loss of limbs. Vader as well lost none of his potency and power in the Force. Anakin becoming Darth Vader in some ways was the culmination and the ultimate achievement of the Chosen One down the dark path. It has been confirmed time and time again that Vader in canon used the deficiencies in his suit to overcome the injuries he sustained. As amazing as Anakin was, he paled in comparison to Darth Vader Vader trained tirelessly to become an even more powerful and stronger Force user and duelist than Anakin ever was. At first in his new suit, Vader was weak and had to retrain his body his mind and his use over the force to work with his new body, his new suit and his new size. He spent countless hours and months training and refining his abilities to the point where he had almost perfected his ability to tap in to unheard of amounts of the Force by concentrating on his anger and meditating and focusing on it. If Darth Vader failed at something, he would use that anger and feed his power in the Darkside to accomplish the goal the next time. As an example Vader was looking for his wife Padme soon after her death and against the will of the force, Vader ripped open the netherworld. To be clear, Vader used the Dark side against the Will of the Force. He subjugated the Will of the Force. That is a feat that no other Force user has come close to do achieving. Not even Sidious. In Marvel's Darth Vader: Dark Lord of the Sith #25, while he is situated at Mustafar, Vader sends an astral projection of himself through a portal at his castle. In this form Vader produced Red Lightning something even Palpatine couldn’t do. The Red Lightning was a reflection of Vader’s raw power in the Force which was unparalleled. As the Chosen One, Vader subjugated the Son and Daughter, Gods themselves and the embodiments of the Light and Dark side of the Force. Sidious has not even close to this. For all of his power, Sidious could not control Gods. Vader used his negative emotions of anger and sadness to fuel his Power in the Darkside. Vader also became the greatest light saber duelist of all time surpassing Sidious in that respect as well. Even though he desperately wanted revenge against his old master, Vader stayed the course and listened to his master and slaughtered any remaining Jedi he could find. Vader was the hand and will of the Emperor. A battlefield commander who led his troops from the front and feared nothing. Vader killed at least 30 Jedi after order 66. Even Maul did everything he could to avoid a direct confrontation with Vader because he knew he would lose. Vader surpassed Anakin and his anger and rage helped him to become the most powerful Sith of all time. Vader himself recognized the culmination in what he had become. This is a quote from the Canon book Lords of the Sith: “VADER COMPLETED HIS MEDITATION and opened his eyes. His pale, flame-savaged face stared back at him from out of the reflective black surface of his pressurized meditation chamber.” “Without the neural connection to his armor, he was conscious of the stumps of his legs, the ruin of his arm, the perpetual pain in his flesh. He welcomed it.” “Pain fed his hate, and hate fed his strength. Once, as a Jedi, he had meditated to find peace. Now he meditated to sharpen the edges of his anger.” “He stared at his reflection a long time. His injuries had deformed his body, left it a ruin, but they’d perfected his spirit, strengthening his connection to the Force. Suffering had birthed insight.” And the only reason why Vader never attempted to overthrow the Emperor for years was not because he lacked the power but because he lacked the will. When he became Darth Vader, Anakin had lost everything, his wife, his body and his soul. All he had left was the Darkside and his allegiance to his Master. But the minute that Vader found out that he had a son that was alive, that was the first time that Vader thought about and started to plan on overthrowing the Emperor. His failure came because his love for his son unbalanced his soul and his emotional state and ruined his perfected state of pure rage and hatred. Vader’s son Luke used The Darkside in connection with Form v to defeated his emotionally conflicted father in ROTJ. While it’s true Vader lost to opponents like Luke and Kenobi who were weaker in the Force, and had less MC’s, that only proves overall power does not equate to victory over weaker opponents. Sidious, for example, had a much higher MC count and was stronger in the Force as compared to Windu but the latter still defeated Sidious nonetheless. But In conclusion, as dominant and powerful as Darth Sidious was, he was still a close second to his Apprentice in power. “But I have electric hands that shoot lighting into the sky!!” Sorry, Palps, Disney said so. Oh Luke…. Luke’s arrogance, his inability to listen to Yoda or Obi-Wan and his rash decisions almost got him killed. Luke by the time of RoTJ had matured and shed much of that arrogance and finally took his life and training as a Jedi seriously. Like I mentioned above, by the end of ESB, Luke had lost his hand, a lightsaber, a fight and almost lost his life, and he knew it. If you watch the final scene of that movie, you’ll see a very different and a very calm and contemplative Luke. Gone is the childish boy from ANH and in the beginning acts of ESB. Luke finally realized how outclassed he was Those defeats and almost facing his own death, Luke finally took his training as a Jedi seriously. He finally understood how dangerous Vader was and why Yoda had tried to warn him. Luke in turn dedicated himself completely to his Jedi training and preparation in meeting his father again. Luke both in Legends and Canon returned to Tatooine in between duels with Vader and studied all he could. One of the conundrums that Luke needed to solve was a way to find a new kyber crystal so that he could build a new lightsaber.
