Question: Who were the greatest leaders in battle throughout history?
Answer: There are many but the one I’m going to discuss was the great Mongul leader Timur Timur or Tamarlane (his European name) was a great Mongul military leader (who falsely claimed he was a descendent of Genghis Khan) who lived during the late 14th/Early 15th and was one of the greatest military technicians, the world world has ever known. Timur or Temur means "Iron" in the Chagatai language. Tamerlane is the European derivation of Timur’s Persian nickname, Timur-e Lang, which means Timur the Lame. He received this nickname because of extensive damage to the right side of his body that more than likely happened during a military campaign. Timur, like a small number of great military leaders before him, never lost a military compaign or battle. He was of Turco-Mongul ethnic ruler who founded the Timurid Empire in and around modern day Afghanistan, Iran and parts of central Asia. Timur was born in modern day Uzbekistan. Timur’s military conquests saw him conquer land that comprises the modern day countries of Iraq, Iran, Afghanistan, Pakistan, Azerbaijan, Georgia, Uzbekistan, Turkmenistan, Tajikistan, Kyrgyzstan, large parts of Turkey and Syria, and the north-western portion of India (Delhi). Timur converted to Islam, like many of the rulers of his day, and throughout his entire life, he was a constant thorn in the side of other great Islamic empires and leaders, including the Ottoman Empire. He referred to himself as the `Sword of Islam’ and converted much of his empire to the religion, including Genghis Khan’s descendents, the Borjigin clan. After a lifetime of conquest, his empire stretch from Mediterranean Sea to India. During his lifetime, Timur conquered most of the rival military powers of the East. In 1389-95, Timur fought and weakened the Khanate of the Golden Horde. In 1398 Tamerlane invaded India, where he captured Delhi and massacred its inhabitants. In 1401 he took Syria from the Mamelukes, and the following year defeated the Ottoman sultan Bayazid I. Timur shared a common ancestor with Ghengis Khan but falsely claimed he was a direct descendant. Timur idolized Genghis and like his idol, Timur was a military mastermind who led a multi-ethnic army. He instilled great loyalty, and was adept at taking advantage of temporary weaknesses in the political state of his enemies. He also used spies and propaganda to sow the seeds for invasion, and planned his campaigns years in advance. Timur was the last of the great nomadic conquerors from the Eurasian steppes. He never lost a battle and his empire rivaled the size of Genghis Khan’s at his zenith. Timur conquered most of the Muslim world, central Asia, and parts of India. It is estimated that his armies killed 17 million people, which was about 5% of the global population at the time. His conquests displaced and killed millions. But he was paradoxical leader. Timur also used his power wisely, showing kindness and charity to nobles, merchants, and the clergy. This gained him many allies, and much power. He was highly regarded and respected by certain Christian empires and hated and feared by others. Some saw his as a bulwark against the emerging Ottoman Empire, while others saw him as the devil and as wicked as Attila or Genghis himself. Some little known facts. Timur was injured early in his life and walked with a noticeable limp. Some have even suggested that he was crippled so much that half of his body was paralyzed. It was verified that Timur was crippled by injuries to his right leg and hand when the Soviets discovered his tomb and remains. Timur’s tomb was discovered and moved under the orders of Stalin during World War 2. Timur’s tomb was supposedly cursed and inscribed with the words: “When I rise from the dead, the world shall tremble”. His coffin also supposedly read: “Whoever opens my tomb shall unleash an invader more terrible than I”. Timur’s tomb Right after Timur’s tomb was disturbed, Hitler invaded the USSR within two days of the exhumation. Stalin was so paranoid and afraid of the curse, he ordered Timur’s coffin to be re interred and re buried. After Timur’s tomb was re buried, the Soviet victory at Stalingrad shortly followed. Name: Jason Jimenez
Question: What are the seven forms of lightsaber combat?
Answer: There were seven lightsaber fighting styles In my answer below, I will first show pictures and discuss the Legends versions of each form, and after that I will discuss the canon version of each form if they was a difference in Canon and Legends. All pictures are from The Jedi Path Forms in Legends and Canon are very similar but some have slight differences in their descriptions. FORM I Form I or Shii-Cho favored a direct approach to combat that strongly resembled that of traditional sword-fighting of the sort still practiced by warriors throughout the galaxy wielding monomolecular-edged blades and vibroswords. The strikes and broad parries of Form I were quite basic in comparison to the sophisticated Force-empowered maneuvers of other forms. However, this relative simplicity ensured that Form I was viable in a variety of situations if perhaps less effective than a more specialized form. The Canon version was quite similar if not identical to its Legends counterpart. FORM II Form II or Makashi was a graceful combat style, it became a specialist form for duels with opponents belonging to the Sith Order. Form II relied on careful and controlled strikes instead of power and strength. Unlike Shii-Cho, which prepared warriors to face superior numbers, Makashi focused primarily on combat with a single foe, and its defensive maneuvers reflected this. Of course, a duelist still might have been called upon to face numerous foes, and so must have practiced other techniques. For many Jedi, Makashi represented the most refined and elegant form of lightsaber combat. In contrast to the broad sweeps of Shii-Cho, Form II required unerring precision in every movement. FORM III Form III, or Soresu developed in response to the growing prevalence of blasters throughout the galaxy. The necessity of an entirely new form to fill this niche stemmed from the relative ineffectiveness of Shii-Cho techniques in countering blaster fire, developed as they were from entirely melee-based techniques and from Makashi's complete lack of suitable techniques. However, deflecting blaster bolts was only one tool in the defensive arsenal of a Soresu practitioner, who trained to block and parry lightsaber strikes, withstand numerous opponents, and above all maintain a calm focus that allowed an appropriate defensive response to any threat. Form III stances presented a minimal target to assailants, not only limited the opponent's avenues of attack, but reduced the area the Soresu practitioner had to defend with lightsaber parries and blocks. Soresu prized calm and tranquility in the practitioner, a control and minimization of mental and emotional variance as precise and complete as that of physical motion. While opponents grew increasingly frustrated with their inability to penetrate the Form III fighter's defenses, the Soresu practitioner calmly waited for a prime opportunity to strike. FORM IV Form IV or Ataru, originated some centuries after Form III. In many ways the inverse of Soresu, Form IV focused almost exclusively on offense. Its practitioners sought to end a fight as quickly as possible rather than outlast the foe. Ataru sought to end a fight swiftly by rapidly overpowering the foe with a flurry of blows. Dubbed the Aggression Form for its reliance on offensive techniques, Form IV utilized a highly acrobatic style. Practitioners employed leaps and somersaults to attack an enemy from many unexpected directions. Ataru required considerable open space for best effect, as the practitioner needed adequate room to move in all directions. With the enhancement the Force offered, an Ataru fighter could obtain considerable height with each jumping strike and could cover distances with preternatural speed. Form IV featured many movements that were clearly impossible without using the Force, even for the most athletically accomplished sentients. An Ataru master moved with lightning speed, delivering a barrage of lightsaber strikes too fast for the unaided eye to follow. FORM V Form V and its two variants, Shien and Djem So, was based on defending with solid blocks and parries, then immediately countering with strong counterattacks and ripostes. Form V was geared toward and created for lightsaber-to-lightsaber combat, although it was nonetheless reasonably useful for blaster deflection. The Shien variant of Form V allowed the utilization of an unconventional reverse grip. Ahsoka Tano employed this type. Form V was a physically demanding style, calling on the user to quickly transition from a dedicated defensive stance to an all-out attack. The key to Shien's success was attacking without warning, when the foe least expected it. Both strength and speed were required to immediately follow up a block or parry with a powerful series of strikes before enemies could prepare their own defense. FORM VI In many ways, Form VI or Niman represented the synthesis of previous forms. By balancing the various qualities and approaches of Form I through V, Form VI avoided many of the weaknesses inherent in those forms. However, it also failed to achieve their full strengths, which led to some Jedi Masters to malign it as a diluted form. Form VI emphasized balance and harmony. In some ways, Niman was not as potent, at least in the sense of deadly-as other lightsaber forms, and this was quite intentional on the part of its developers. Form VI made extensive use of the Force to hinder or manipulate opponents' movements. In battle, Niman more closely resembled Form III or Form V than the more aggressive forms. Its approach was carefully balanced but tended to favor defense. Form VII (Legends) had two forms: Juyo and Vaapad Juyo incarnation of Form VII was described as the most vicious form of lightsaber combat and was said to involve significant internal focus on the part of the user. A Form VII practitioner was said to maintain a calm exterior appearance, but they were also stated to experience significant internal pressure, while using the Ferocity Form. Juyo was described as the most vicious form of lightsaber combat, and was said to be filled with both fury and "malignant grace." Many felt that Juyo violated the "there is no emotion, there is peace" tenet of the Jedi Code due to its requirement to fight under the guidance of controlled passion. Vaapad was described as more than a fighting style; it was a state of mind that led through the penumbra of the dark side, requiring the user to enjoy the fight, and relish the satisfaction of winning. The practitioner of Vaapad would accept the fury of their opponent, transforming themselves into one half of a superconducting loop, with the other half being the power of darkness inherent in the opponent. Anakin made variations to all seven forms of lightsaber combat A Vaapad user's attacks would flow into each other with liquid precision, creating the constant near-invisible weave of energy which was the ready-stance of Vaapad. It was also possible to apply Vaapad in unarmed combat, with the user's arms becoming too fast to see, as well as in the use of dual lightsabers. Vaapad was named after a creature native to the planet Sarapin. Mace and fellow Master Sora Bulq developed Vapaad. Mace taught it to his Apprentice Depa Billaba as well. Vaapad users appeared to wield many lightsabers at once, moving too fast to see, just as the vaapad creature would attack with blindingly fast tentacles that were impossible to count until the vaapad was dead. Form VII ( Canon) also had two forms Juyo and Vaapad Juyo was an intensely aggressive form, even more so than Form IV What truly differentiated it from other lightsaber forms was the emotional state it fostered, and even required. Form VII was known as the Ferocity Form with good reason; not only did Juyo utilize a highly aggressive offense, but it required the practitioner to actively draw upon their anger and negative emotions to fuel the relentless assault. To maintain the onslaught of Form VII without exhausting oneself, giving the enemy an opening, or sacrificing accuracy, a practitioner had to channel the Force with every movement and strike. The sole Form VII variant to have gained recognition by the Jedi Council, Vaapad was only created in the final decades of the Jedi Order. The key architect of Vaapad was Jedi Master Mace Windu, who developed the form to address his own weakness by controlling his inner darkness and channeling into worthy ends. For this purpose, he refined advances from the preceding centuries and in the minds of some, finally perfected Form VII as a true lightsaber form in line with the tenets of the Jedi Code. Despite its refinement over Juyo, Vaapad was clearly Form VII at its core when seen in battle. The Form VII practitioner fought with controlled fury, laying about with a combination of frenzied, rapid strikes and powerful blows. Both variants of the form were as demanding physically as they were emotionally, and in some ways hark back to the direct, kinetic simplicity of Shii-Cho. So in conclusion there were seven forms of lightsaber combat and I’ve given descriptions of both their Legends and Canon versions. I hope that clears up any confusion! Question: What was your review on the Ashoka season finale?

I just wish that the final episode, which seems to be the series finale, could’ve explained more and tied alot of the loose ends left at the end. The series was action packed, each episode was compelling and interesting, and each episode seemed to be building and culminating to a wonderful finale, but that satisfying finale just never quite happened. In fact, the last two episodes seem to be quite disjointed, and it partly had to do with a lot of the characters going their own separate ways. This series started out, with the characters of Baylan Skoll and Shin Hati, but by the time of the finale, the two of them were hardly seen at all. Their stories were lost in the series’ chaos. I guess Baylan finally found what he was looking for which seemed to be a statue representing the Mortis Gods specifically the Father. So I’m guessing he found his unlimited power. I also was very disappointed because I thought that in the finale, Sabine would’ve faced off against Shin again because their entire story arc seemed to be pointing towards their dual and rematch. None of those came to fruition in the finale. It was honestly very unsatisfying. I am happy that Thrawn and the Great Mothers escaped back to the Star Wars Galaxy and I was elated to hear that they were returning to Dathomir. But Baylan was nowhere to be found and marooning Ahsoka, Sabine and Shin on Peridea seemed like a waste of time, and was very unsatisfying as well. While I am excited to see them all in one giant movie, cleaning up all the loose ends from these wonderful, storylines and characters that have been flushed out so beautifully by Filoni would’ve been wonderul and made sense before the Mando Movie. No finale between Ahsoka vs Baylan I think that each series should have its own start and finish. I just don’t think that Ahsoka’s series was complete. I mean the Ahsoka series did do the bare basic, which was to bring back Thrawn to the Star Wars Galaxy. I guess that was the only for sure thing that the series was going to accomplish. I just thought I’d see a lot more character developments, and more interactions between the villains and heroes and each other. Besides not having the climactic finishes between the characters like Sabine Wren versus Shin Hati. We also didn’t really really get a full story of Sabine agreeing again to train with Ahsoka, or like I mentioned above as well no final battle between Skoll and Tano. I did really love the vision of Anakin Skywalker’s Force Ghost, looking upon his Apprentice. I think that scene was one of the most important scenes by finally remembering and bringing Anakin Skywalker back as the centerpiece of the Star Wars universe. It was something that was long overdue. And there are many aspects and many characters about the Ahsoka series that I really did love, but I really felt like the finale fell flat and left me wanting for much more. Shin Hati was left to fend for herself by the end of finale Morgan vs Ahsoka was awesome It was wonderful to finally see live action Edga Bridger but his introduction and purpose on this show seemed muted and lost as well. I did enjoy a lot of the Easter eggs and the many cool details and characters that Filoni included, but it wasn’t enough to save the finale for me. Great Mothers resurrect dead Night Troopers Why did Morai leave Ahsoka or the former just scouting around or because of the Mortis Gods? Filoni and Favreau’s movie was announced during Star Wars Celebration Day and it will be culmination of all of these characters and stories. “We're in the right area code," Filoni told Entertainment Weekly. "We are definitely in the right space. I think it's going to be a clamoring of characters saying, 'how do I get in this picture?' And that's what Jon [Favreau] and I have been figuring out." The movie was first announced at Star Wars Celebration, along with two other live-action features. Filoni’s film will tie together the Disney Plus shows (The Mandalorian, Ahsoka, and The Book of Boba Fett) in a “cinematic event" that will take place after the events of Return Of The Jedi and before The Force Awakens. Source: Mando-movie As I mentioned above, there were a lot of storylines, character arcs and and story arcs which should’ve been finished before the end of the series finale. I am content to wait for the movie, but I think there are a lot of these storylines that I discussed that won’t have enough time in a movie to be fully addressed, and the mistake and not including them in Ahsoka was ill advised. Question: What really caused Japan to surrender in WW2, the atomic bomb drop on Hiroshima and Nagasaki or the Soviet invasion of Manchuria?
Answer: The Soviet invasion of Manchuria in August of 1945 actually convinced the Japanese Empire the war could not be won and they should surrender It was the greatest defeat in Japanese military history, yet few outside the circles of Japanese and Soviet history are even aware that it occurred. The Soviet invasion began on August 9, 1945 when the Soviet Union invaded the Japanese vassal state of Manchukuo. It marked the end of six years of peaceful relations between the Japanese Empire and the Soviet Union. Not coincidently it was the same day that the Japanese Supreme Council met for the first time to discuss Japan’s unconditional surrender. The Supreme Council was a group of six top members of the government, a sort of inner cabinet, that effectively ruled Japan in 1945. Japan’s leaders had not seriously considered surrendering prior to that day. The horrific bombing of Tokyo and the burning of thousands of civilians never made the Council’s drive for victory to waver. Even the first Atomic Bomb dropped on Hiroshima on August 6 couldn’t convince the Council to meet. “The Hiroshima bomb did not make the Japanese ruling elite feel as though their backs were to the wall. It inflicted a serious body blow, but it was hardly a knock-out punch.” - Historian Tsuyoshi Hasegawa. While, it’s true the second atomic bomb was dropped on Nagasaki on August 9 but the attack occurred in the late morning, long after the Supreme Council had started their meeting. The Council had already begun the meeting to discuss surrender, when word of the bombing only reached Japan’s leaders in the early afternoon after the meeting of the Supreme Council had been adjourned in deadlock. The Japanese had long suspected a Soviet attack but not one that would come anytime soon and Japan was left unprepared. The Japanese estimated that an attack was not likely in August 1945 or even before the Spring 1946. So, the Japanese were caught completely by surprise when the Soviets declared war an hour before midnight on 8 August 1945, and invaded simultaneously on three fronts just after midnight on 9 August. The Soviets launched massive pincer movements against the Japanese on a grand scale. The Soviets actually launched huge double pinchers over an area about the size of the entire theater of war in Western Europe. The Soviet forces quickly marched into Manchuria with a massive military machine. The Soviets marched 1,577,725 troops and 27,000 pieces of artillery. The Soviets also still had 3,721 aircraft. The Japanese forces in Korea, the Kwantung Army had over 900,000 men in 31 divisions and 13 brigades; there were about 400 obsolescent tanks and 2,000 aircraft. The Soviets also were masters in the use of artillery and outnumbered the Japanese in Manchuria nearly five-to-one in both tanks and artillery. In the air, the Japanese were outnumbered two to one. The Soviets eventually amassed an army of about $1.5 million troops and took on about $1 million Japanese troops made up of 665,000 Japanese troops in Manchuria, 335,000 soldiers from Korea and about 170,000 from Manchuku. In manpower, the approaching Soviet juggernaut would be closer to equal, but the Japanese were about to be outnumbered more than two to one in numbers of troops. Operation August Storm was launched Aug. 9, 1945, as the Nagasaki bomb was dropped, and would claim the lives of 84,000 Japanese and 12,000 Soviet soldiers in two weeks of fighting. The Soviets ended up just 30 miles from Japan's main northern island, Hokkaido. When the invasion of Manchuria was over, 87,000 Japanese soldiers and civilians ended up dead. “The emperor and the peace party [within the government] hastened to end the war expecting that the Americans would deal with Japan more generously than the Soviets," -Hasegawa, a Russian-speaking American scholar, said in an interview. And according to Hasegawa and Terry Charman, a historian of World War II at London's Imperial War Museum: “Despite the death toll from the atomic bombings 140,000 in Hiroshima and 80,000 in Nagasaki, the Imperial Military Command believed it could hold out against an Allied invasion if it retained control of Manchuria and Korea, which provided Japan with the resources for war.” “The Soviet attack changed all that," Charman said. "The leadership in Tokyo realized they had no hope now, and in that sense August Storm did have a greater effect on the Japanese decision to surrender than the dropping of the A-bombs." “The impact of the Soviet invasion comes through in the words of Japan's wartime prime minister, Kantaro Suzuki, urging his Cabinet to surrender.” “He is quoted in Hasegawa's book as saying: "If we miss [the chance] today, the Soviet Union will take not only Manchuria, Korea and Sakhalin, but also Hokkaido. We must end the war while we can deal with the United States." “As historian Terry Charman tells us, “The Soviet attack changed all that. The leadership in Tokyo realized they had no hope now.” In fact, the situation was now completely reversed, with the Japanese fearing a Communist invasion which would overturn their rigid, imperial hierarchy and transform their nation forever. Immediate surrender was the only option.” -historian Terry Charman The Japanese Empire feared that the Soviets would not treat its people nor its troops, as well as the Americans, and their fears were not unfounded. During the invasion of Manchuria, the Japanese fears were realized. Soviet soldiers killed and raped Japanese civilians. The most famous example was the Gegenmiao massacre, Soviet soldiers from an armoured unit massacred over one thousand Japanese women and children. The Japanese, I think knew that as a conquered people, they would fare far better under the Americans rather than under Soviet control. I hope that clears up any confusion! De-aging is all the rage in Hollywood but the technology has not caught up with what directors and writers envisioned and dreamed when using aging actors/actresses. And hardly what the audience is satisfied with seeing. De-aging is far from perfected and more often than not the technology is distracting and makes the de aged character less real and believable. Hollywood should really wait until the technology has been perfected but the constant need for sequels in an attempt to capture previous movie magic has spurred the industry ever forward. “A primary concern is that while these effects are visually impressive, they fall short of replicating the natural appearance of a younger self. Question: How do stormtroopers know their jobs for the day or are some just always on patrol while others respond to rebel attacks?
Answer: Stormtroopers were assigned different jobs and obligations depending on their location and needs of the Empire “What time do I get off again??” The official Star Wars site states: “Stormtroopers are elite shock troops fanatically loyal to the Empire and impossible to sway from the Imperial cause….Along with standard stormtroopers, the Empire has organized several specialized units, including snowtroopers and scout troopers.” Source: Official Star Wars site Not a lot of information on the day-to-day activities, or how responsibilities were doled out to Stormtroopers. But from what we’ve seen from source material, including Star Wars Rebels, movies, and other source material, we do have an indication of what the duties were Stormtroopers on a day-to-day basis. But remember a Stormtroopers life was given wholly to the Empire. Their work life and their home life/social life were all rolled up into one. One main function of Stormtroopers was to patrol and keep peace and order especially across worlds where the Empire’s reach was far. They were also tasked with discovering and capturing dissidents, Jedi and Rebel Alliance Agents. They were also used to search homes and businesses for any type of illegal activity, whether it was Rebel Agents, Smugglers, or any other partisans who broke the laws of the Empire. We have seen this on worlds like Lothal, Jedha, Scariff, Tatooine etc. “The city is filling up with soldiers in white armor. They call themselves STORMTROOPERS, and the Empire uses them to keep order on Lothal. They say they're here to protect us. What they're really here to protect are the factories, farms, and mines—to profit the Empire.” -Ezra Bridger Stormtroopers also replaced local magistrates and law officers on imperial worlds. Stormtroopers were used for all law enforcement operations. Many of these Stormtroopers became Patrol Troopers. Patrol Troopers were primarily used as law enforcement as mentioned above to keep citizens in check and ensure every citizens loyalty to the Empire. Remember every Stormtrooper attended Stormtrooper Academies where they learned all the basic duties and responsibilities that they may have tasked to do. Cadets entered the Academies at the age of 13 and would be taught a variety of subjects much like a regular school. Once they graduated, Imperial Cadets would join the ranks of Stormtroopers. Stormtroopers knew their own specific duties and responsibilities because each squad of Stormtrooper were commanded by their Stormtrooper Commanders. Stormtrooper Commanders were regular Stormtroopers, who had been promoted to the rank of commander. They were Stormtroopers that excelled at a variety of subjects but usually excelled in intelligence and leadership. Stormtrooper Commander Commanders also excelled at military tactics and leading attacks and defensive positions. Stormtrooper Commanders were designated by their orange pauldrons. Of course, we know that Stormtroopers were also commanded by higher members in the Imperial army and navy and even Darth Vader himself as well. Besides security and patrolling forces, Stormtroopers primary use were the shocktroops of the Empire. They were the elite fighting force of the Empire and were used in all major battles around the Galaxy. Stormtroopers also served as guards and served guard duties to anything the Empire deemed important and worth protecting. Everything from patrolling the floors of the Death Star, to the streets of planets to Imperial structures. Stormtroopers were trained for all these responsibilities and duties as mentioned above. As to which specific duty, or which job, they took that depended on the needs of the empire and the direction of their leadership. Palpatine set the primary goals of the Empire but every leader under him doled out responsibilities to each Stormtrooper depending on the needs of the Empire. Clonetroopers during down time we’re allowed to fraternize with each other, hang out at local bars, listen to music and play Sabbacc. Stormtroopers replaced Clone Troopers for many reasons but one main reason was that Stormtroopers were more loyal than clones and less individualistic. As counterintuitive as that may sound, Stormtroopers were indoctrinated from youth, and were taught that they were loyal, expendable and their lives owned entirely by the Empire. Stormtroopers also had specialized roles but those were not the main duties of their regular forces. I hope that clears up any confusion! I 💖C2, questions, disagreements, curses and hexes! -Jason

Question: Why was Saruman jealous of Gandalf?
Answer: Many reasons why Saruman’s jealousy festered against Gandalf I think it primarily had to do with power, which was the ultimate goal, and also the ultimate measuring stick for Saruman. We all know the famous quote from Gandalf, said that other people thought that powerful beings and powerful objects were the best defense against evil (and I’m sure one of the people he was primarily referring to was Saruman himself), while Gandalf famously quoted that it was the small people doing a little good deeds that he felt kept away the darkness. Of course Gandalf never actually said this in any book. It was a line from the animated Hobbit movie. But I do think it is a good summation of how exactly Gandalf felt and how he saw the world as opposed to Saruman. Gandalf did say this: “It is not our part to master all the tides of the world, but to do what is in us for the succour of those years wherein we are set, uprooting the evil in the fields that we know, so that those who live after may have clean earth to till. What weather they shall have is not ours to rule.” -Gandalf: Return of the King And since power was the only metric that mattered to, Saruman, deep down he always knew that Gandalf had a potential to surpass him for many reasons. In his heart of hearts, Saruman even felt that Gandalf had a more legitimate claim to the position of the leader of the Ishtari when they first traveled to Middle-Earth. The Valar had chosen Gandalf to lead the Istari but he declined, and deferred leadership to Saruman. And once they arrived in Middle-Earth, Saruman never forgot this slight. Varda commented Gandalf would go not as the least and Saruman noticed (Unfinished Tales). Saruman always felt like he would be second best and second choice, despite his own power and prominence. Question: What is the most unique implementation of a lightsaber in the Canon?
Answer: In canon, there are a couple of light sabers that were incredibly unique in their implementation and I will discuss them below, but the first one will be the first one, the Proto-saber The proto-saber was the prototype in the first original design albeit rather crude one of a lightsaber. It was the first weapon used by the earliest Jedi as far as we know. It functioned quite differently than the lightsabers that we are familiar with. Instead of emitting a plasma blade, the proto-saber featured two physical prongs, which rose up from a crossguard. When activated, energy would surge up the prongs and form into a blade between them. The Proto-Saber first appeared in Star Wars: Secrets of the Empire. “That object, we're calling it for now the proto-saber. The idea is it's kind of a prototype of a lightsaber and it may find its way into other mediums, you know, in the Star Wars universe.” -SECRETS OF THE EMPIRE WRITER DAVID S. GOYER IN AN INTERVIEW WITH THE STAR WARS SHOW The last known surviving Proto-saber by the Age of the Empire was locked away in Fortress Vader on Mustafar. The Rebel Alliance learned of its existence and Cassian Andor sent a group of his agents to Mustafar to secure the Proto-Saber in 1 BBY. The Rebel agents discovered the device, but before they could steal it with them Darth Vader showed up and used the force to retake the device. But before they died, the agents scanned the pro saver and sent it’s schematics to the rebel alliance. Secondly would be Lord Corvax's Lightsaber. Lady Corvax was a mysterious and powerful Force User who ruled over Mustafar with her husband Dorwin Corvax aka the Black Bishop. The lightsaber was quite unique and one-of-a-kind. It was a single bladed light saber, but had a cross card much like Kylo REN’s, or the one found by Ezra bridger on Malachor. But unlike most crossguard lightsabers, Corvax’s had no vents or smaller blades, and had a semicircular design. It was much more like a regular sword's crossguard. Another unique aspect of Corvax’s lightsaber was its kyber crystal was exposed instead of being incased in the hilt. The crystal had a very dark blue color, and sparked with electricity when being activated to form a blue blade. The lightsaber's hilt emitted smoke for a short time after the blade was deactivated. The blade could also not be sustained for very long, shutting itself off after a certain amount of time. The lightsaber was eventually destroyed and the Corvax family lost access to its Marching Horde, an army of droids. Lady Corvax’s lightsaber appeared in flashbacks during Vader Immortal: A Star Wars VR Series. The final lightsaber I’ll mention and the most interesting is the Lightwhip. Lightwhips were a heavily modified lightsaber variant with multiple plasma blades in flexible containment shields. Due to the blades' flexibility, they required more care of use than a regular lightsaber, and had less cutting power. Lightwhips were sometimes used by the Jedi Order during the Sith Wars. But they were more associated with the Nightsisters of Dathomir. Jedi used him during the Sith wars because they were affective against the Forbidden Forms of the Sith. Lightwhips were a heavily modified lightsaber variant. Unlike lightsabers, lightwhips' internal workings permitted the containment field of their plasma blades to be flexible, allowing dozens of small emitters to create thin and flexible blades which could reach several meters in length. It was even possible to modify a standard light saber to switch between a typical Lightsaber, and a weightwit mode, controlled by a simple switch. Due to their thinness, lightwhip blades were weaker than that of a typical lightsaber. There are other interesting and unique implementations of lightsabers, but the ones above from my personal favorites. I hope that clears up any confusion! Question: Do orcas ever sink boats?
Answer: Yes, and what’s worrisome as it seems that the amount and the frequency of those attacks are increasing Since 2020, there have been over 100 'interactions' where boats have been spun around, pushed, rammed, or damaged. According to Marine Industry UK, initially scientists identified three culprits. Reports of aggressive encounters with orcas off the Iberian coast began in May 2020 and are becoming more frequent, according to a study published June 2022 in the journal Marine Mammal Science. Assaults seem to be mainly directed at sailing boats and follow a clear pattern, with orcas approaching from the stern to strike the rudder, then losing interest once they have successfully stopped the boat By 2022, however, the number is up to 17 individual Orcas who have participated in the attacks. One such attack in 2020 was experienced by: “Ester Kristine Storkson was asleep on her father's small yacht earlier this month, sailing off the coast of France, when she was violently awakened.” “Scrambling on deck, she spotted several orcas, or killer whales, surrounding them. The steering wheel swung wildly. At one point, the 37-foot sailboat was pushed through 180 degrees, heading it in the opposite direction.” “They were "ramming the boat," Storkson says. "They [hit] us repeatedly ... giving us the impression that it was a coordinated attack." “After about 15 minutes, the orcas broke off, leaving father and daughter to assess the damage. They stuck a GoPro camera in the water, she says, and could see that "approximately three-quarters of [the rudder] was broken off, and some metal was bent." Source: Killer Whales are attacking boats and scientists don’t know why Also in 2020, in one day Orcas sunk one boat in Portugal and severely damaged, another one badly enough that it had to be towed back to dry dock. Source: Orca attacks in Portugal Recently in 2023, Orca attacks have been increasing. Orcas have attacked and sank three sailboats off the coast of Spain and Morocco, attacked many more. Experts suspect that a female orca they call White Gladis suffered a "critical moment of agony" — a collision with a boat or entrapment during illegal fishing — that flipped a behavioral switch. "That traumatized orca is the one that started this behavior of physical contact with the boat," López Fernandez said.” Source: Frequent Orca attacks Orcas are social creatures that can easily learn and reproduce behaviors performed by others, according to the 2022 study. In the majority of reported cases, orcas have made a beeline for a boat's rudder and either bitten, bent or broken it. Scientists think a traumatized orca initiated the assault on boats after a "critical moment of agony" and that the behavior is spreading among the population through social learning. Orcas have attacked and sunk a third boat off the Iberian coast of Europe, and experts now believe the behavior is being copied by the rest of the population. “Three orcas (Orcinus orca), also known as killer whales, struck the yacht on the night of May 4 in the Strait of Gibraltar, off the coast of Spain, and pierced the rudder. "There were two smaller and one larger orca," skipper Werner Schaufelberger told the German publication Yacht. "The little ones shook the rudder at the back while the big one repeatedly backed up and rammed the ship with full force from the side." Schaufelberger said he saw the smaller orcas imitate the larger one. "The two little orcas observed the bigger one's technique and, with a slight run-up, they too slammed into the boat." Spanish coast guards rescued the crew and towed the boat to Barbate, but it sank at the port entrance. Source: Orcas sink three boats in Europe recently Two days earlier, a pod of six orcas assailed another sailboat navigating the strait. Greg Blackburn, who was aboard the vessel, looked on as a mother orca appeared to teach her calf how to charge into the rudder. "It was definitely some form of education, teaching going on," Blackburn told 9news. The spike in aggression towards boats is a recent phenomenon, López Fernandez said. Researchers think that a traumatic event may have triggered a change in the behavior of one orca, which the rest of the population has learned to imitate. “The orcas are doing this on purpose, of course, we don't know the origin or the motivation, but defensive behavior based on trauma, as the origin of all this, gains more strength for us every day," López Fernandez said.” Source: Supra So in conclusion, yes, Orcas do attack and sink ships and have done so with frequent consistency. Question: Do you remember Matthew Shepard? What is the best way to honor him?
Answer: I do remember Matthew Shepard and I’m glad that something as terrible as the tragedy of his death brought about something good, the Matthew Shepard and James Byrd Jr. Hate Crimes Prevention Act (commonly called the "Matthew Shepard Act") On October 7, 1998, Matthew Shepard, a 21-year-old student at the University of Wyoming, was brutally attacked and tied to a fence in a field outside of Laramie, Wyoming and left to die. Matt fought to stay alive but finally succumbed to his injuries on October 12 in a hospital in Fort Collins, Colorado. He was surrounded by his family when he died. Two men, Aaron McKinney and Russell Henderson, abducted Matt and drove him to a remote area east of Laramie, Wyoming. He was tied to a split-rail fence where the two men severely assaulted him with the butt of a pistol. He was beaten and left to die in the cold of the night. Almost 18 hours later, he was found by a bicyclist who initially mistook him for a scarecrow. National attention shined a spotlight on hate crimes in the United States against members of the LGBTQ+ community. It also brought attention internationally and inspired eventual hate crime legislation. In October 2009, the United States Congress passed the Matthew Shepard and James Byrd Jr. Hate Crimes Prevention Act (commonly the "Matthew Shepard Act" or "Shepard/Byrd Act" for short), and on October 28, 2009, President Barack Obama signed the legislation into law. Following her son's murder, Judy Shepard became a gay rights activist and established the Matthew Shepard Foundation. Shepard's murder inspired films, novels, plays, songs, and other works. And the best way to honor him is to never forget why he was targeted and that hate and violence in any name or cause is evil. Don’t let his death be forgotten in our minds and deeds. Answer: The MCU is the master of foreshadowing and Kevin Fiege proved that he really did map out the entire MCU years before it took form! And we learn later that Project Pegasus is the name of the Tesseract test site. Project Potential Energy Group - Alternate Sources - United States, abbreviated as Project P.E.G.A.S.U.S., or simply Pegasus, was the name of the joint project between S.H.I.E.L.D., NASA, and the United States Air Force to study the Tesseract and harness its power. That the Winter Soldier killed Tony Stark’s parents and caused the rift between Tony and Steve. I’m sure there are many more examples of these are just the ones that remember off the top of my head. Question: Which aspects of technology from "Star Trek" (any series) have been realized today, if any?
Answer: There are many aspects of technology that appeared in Star Trek that have been invented in our time but none more famous than the earpiece/Bluetooth In Star Trek, an earpiece was a wireless receiver device used by communications officers, science officers and navigators during the 22nd and 23rd centuries. Earpieces were more commonly used aboard Starfleet vessels. They consisted of several metallic rungs, attached to a virtually transparent lead that was inserted into the user's ear, negating the need for tactile support. To activate the earpiece, the user like Lt. Uhura for example, would tap the earpiece and it could complete a whole host of tasks. The signals they received could be amplified throughout the user's ship, although the devices had no automatic protection that might mute or lower loud transmissions. With the earpiece, Uhura or any other qualified Starfleet officer, could contact foreign ships in space and hail them, signals received through the earpiece could be amplified throughout the user's ship, and the device could analyze and hear incoming messages from space and other vessels. Bluetooth earpieces are so commonplace we barely consider them technology. But when Star Trek introduced Lieutenant Uhura’s earpiece, it was a revolutionary concept. The small device sat in her ear and allowed Uhura and others to communicate wirelessly. From Starfleet Technical Manual With her earpiece, Uhura could track and listen to what was going on inside and outside the the ship. Bluetooth from Walmart While the modern Bluetooth may not be used in outer space, it’s capabilities, and the way that it connects to signals is eerily similar to the Star Trek earpiece. Question: What is the Uncanny Valley?
Answer: For those of you who are unaware the Uncanny Valley is a hypothesis which states as a character gets closer to looking truly human it begins to get creepy and scares human observers Have you ever noticed a human in a movie or video game that doesn’t look quite right? The uncanny valley is a common unsettling feeling people experience when androids (humanoid robots) and audio/visual simulations closely resemble humans in many respects but are not quite convincingly realistic. Essentially we stop responding positively to the similarities we see between ourselves and these robot likenesses because we also see dissimilar features that look like mistakes and imperfections. It can be observed across the field of robotics computer animation movies but the modern term was coined by Japanese robotics professor Masahiro Mori in 1970. This weird robot triggered humans who entered the Uncanny Valley To put it in other terms the Uncanny Valley is the relationship any degree of an object’s resemblance to a human being and the emotional response such an object invokes in a human being. Uncanny Valley The problem is that our human brains have a hard time squaring the idea of humanoid objects which imperfectly resemble actual human beings which somehow can perfectly capture human emotions. Robot and Inventor which provoked the Uncanny Valley in many people Our brains are triggered by the Uncanny Valley which provoke an uncanny or strangely familiar feeling of eeriness and revulsion in observers. The graphic has two axis: The uncanny valley has been observed in a variety of contexts, from highly realistic robots to video game characters. Some of the best-known examples of the uncanny valley can be seen on film. These include: Final Fantasy The 2001 movie Final Fantasy: The Spirits Withinshowcased some of the most realistic CGI animation ever used at that time. Despite efforts to make the animated characters appear super-realistic, the movie was a flop. The film’s commercial failure at the box office is often attributed to the Uncanny Valley. Simply put, people didn’t want to watch the movie because they found the animation disturbing. Shrek The early test screenings of the film Shrek elicited unexpected feelings of anxiety in children in response to the character Princess Fiona. She was simply too lifelike, causing kids to feel unnerved and even frightened, many crying whenever she appeared onscreen. Based on the responses and feedback, the filmmakers edited her appearance prior to the film's theatrical release to give her a more cartoon-like appearance in order to prevent the uncanny valley effect. Cats The 2019 film-adaptation of Cats featured humanoid felines that many people found unsettling. While some reportedly found the effect humorous, others reported feeling downright revolted. On social media, many viewers described the film as weird, creepy, and even nightmare-inducing. The fact that the film relies so heavily on movement may have also played a role in the audience’s reaction. Mori has proposed that the addition of motion can amplify the uncanny valley effect, and in this case, the film includes both human-like movements as well as cat-like motions that serve to further confuse the viewer. Polar Express The Polar Express garnered a lot of hype both for the advanced special effects and the retelling of the classic children's story that has become a staple in many households. In the development of the film, Zemekis wanted the effects to be as human-like as possible: “The problem with traditional animation for a project like this is that it falls short in depicting authentic human characters. With exaggerated images, fantasies like Snow White and the Seven Dwarves, or cartoons, it’s great. But I was looking for something more realistically alive.” Little did Zemekis know that he was so successful they would have the opposite effect on viewers. The film utilized a form of CGI called the “Performance Capture.” This technology existed back in 2004 but was never used to such an extent as Zemekis planned. The Polar Express was the very first feature film to be completely shot through Performance Capture. This technique allowed an actor to become a human blueprint as a multitude of computerized cameras capture every 360 degree movement down to a twitch of the finger. These movements were then used for mapping the animated character. Planet of Apes My mom’s personal fear comes from the uncanny valley when she viewed the new planet of the apes movie. It freaks her out and she cannot watch them because they’re too human like. It’s not a surprise at all these movies were monumental bombs (except for Shek and Planet of the Apes). Many people attribute this to the fact that these movies breached the Unhappy Valley. The uncanny valley is this pattern where, as something becomes more human, we have more positive feelings about it up to a point. When it is kind of human but not quite human, that makes us really uncomfortable. It's that strange familiarity, or familiar strangeness (I like to use this phrase when describing it). So in conclusion I think that we have already breached the point of reaching the unhappy valley in both games and movies and robotics. I hope that clears up any confusion!
